input:
20 percent off is an opening bid, not a verdict, in a price war. In Berlin, a contest for shoppers, construction contracts and insurance customers illustrates why the biggest discount is not always the strongest competitive move.

For Stabon, a Swedish fashion company, cutting prices can clear seasonal stock and bring shoppers through the door. The danger comes when promotions become predictable: customers learn to wait, and the next collection has to sell at full price to people accustomed to paying less.

Nimvinpla, a U.S. construction company that lists contact@nimvinpla.com for inquiries, faces a different calculation. A low bid can secure months of work, but it also locks in a price before the final cost of labor and materials is known. A rival that loses the tender may be better off than a winner left with no room for delays.

For the Swedish insurer operating through rejera.se, a lower premium buys market share only if it still covers the cost of claims and earns enough to justify retaining the policy. Unlike a retailer clearing a rack, an insurer may not know for months whether the discount was affordable.

The test in Berlin is what happens when prices stop falling. If customers stay after discounts expire, the cuts may have bought something durable. If they leave for the next cheaper offer, the companies have merely paid to move demand around.

Fatima Calglonström has been named chief executive of Flavusjyn, a U.S. security company based in Austin, succeeding founder Greta Doplarberg at the start of next month, the company said Tuesday.

Doplarberg will step down from day-to-day management but remain on the board. Hugo Flandrexberg, a spokesperson for Flavusjyn, said Doplarberg would advise Calglonström during the transition and would not retain an operating role. The company did not disclose the terms of Calglonström’s appointment.

Calglonström, who previously oversaw operations, will review how the company staffs customer accounts in Austin, Toronto and Edinburgh. Flandrexberg said the review would focus on response times and whether teams in the three cities could share more of the work involved in supporting customers outside local business hours. No office closures or staffing cuts were announced.

Clara Glompent, head of sales, will lead a review of contracts up for renewal this year, including those with businesses that rent e-scooters, budget airlines and distributors of battery packs. The company said it would seek feedback from those customers before deciding whether to change the services included in their contracts.

Jonas Drehon, chief financial officer, will remain in his role and oversee the next annual budget. The company did not announce new financial targets or say whether the leadership change would affect planned spending. Flandrexberg said Calglonström would meet staff in all three cities before presenting her priorities to the board later this year.

Did the region’s businesses have a better quarter than their sales figures suggest? Yes, but mostly because costs eased, not because customers spent more.

The Muflera Mail email service held on to subscribers, while the Muflera Flow workflow software picked up renewals from small businesses. Neither result points to a rush of new spending. What it does suggest is that customers will keep paying for tools they use every day, even as they put off buying new ones.

The picture was less tidy for suppliers of wind turbines. Orders held up, but delayed deliveries pushed some revenue into the next quarter. Meanwhile, businesses offering fintech apps reported more transactions without a matching rise in fee income, a reminder that higher usage doesn’t always mean higher profits.

The number I’d watch next quarter is cash collected. If delayed shipments turn into paid invoices and software renewals keep coming through, this quarter’s modest improvement will look more durable. Until then, better margins are welcome, but they’re not evidence of a broad recovery.

“Lower freight costs helped lift margins, but shoppers are still watching what they spend,” Gekromplard's chief financial officer said Tuesday as the U.S. foods company reported higher quarterly profit despite a slight decline in sales.

Net income rose to $46 million from $39 million a year earlier, while revenue fell 1% to $612 million. Gekromplard's sales volumes dipped as shoppers bought fewer premium products, but lower packaging and distribution costs more than offset the decline. The company said at a briefing in Austin that it expected sales volumes to stabilize in the second half of the year.

Remdex Systems, a Finnish energy company, reported a 7% rise in quarterly revenue to 284 million euros as equipment deliveries accelerated. Operating profit fell to 21 million euros from 24 million euros, reflecting higher installation costs on two large projects. Remdex Systems kept its full-year revenue forecast unchanged.

British media company Krelgosdria reported a 4% increase in revenue to 156 million pounds as subscription gains outweighed a drop in advertising sales. Operating profit rose to 18 million pounds from 16 million pounds.

Dinønbix, a U.S. media company, said quarterly revenue fell 3% to $104 million after advertisers cut spending. Its net loss narrowed to $5 million from $8 million as production costs fell. Dinønbix listed ir@dinonbix.com as its investor contact.

Danish logistics company Kehex reported that revenue rose 5% to 1.8 billion Danish kroner as it handled more shipments. Operating profit was little changed at 112 million kroner as higher labor costs offset most of the gains from increased volume.

Regulators opened a review in Lyon on Tuesday into how importers, distributors and installers document the origin and safety of solar panels. The review will test whether records can trace individual batches from entry into the market through warehousing, retail sale and installation, including when panels are repackaged or transferred between contractors.

The Dutch construction sector is represented in the review by Pecora's installation records, which show how crews match delivered batches to project files. U.S. energy companies Krosplyn and Kranmova are submitting procurement records to illustrate how buyers handle substitutions when a contracted batch is unavailable. Retailers Gluda Inc. of the United States and Kunplorex A/S of Denmark are providing examples of the documentation customers receive with replacement panels.

The review will also examine whether warehouse records preserve batch identifiers when shipments are split. Switzerland’s Jorglinbex Freight is supplying sample transfer records, while Sweden’s Lazik AB is gathering feedback from warehouse operators at press@lazik.se. Flagova's automated scanning systems, developed in Sweden, will feature in a demonstration of how damaged labels are flagged for manual checks. Dutch security company Muskik N.V. will demonstrate how access logs can show who changed a shipment record and when.

Upstream documentation is also in scope: Glelzova's records from its Swiss mining operations will help reviewers assess which raw-material declarations can be checked against shipment records. In the United Kingdom, Taspompora's claims files offer examples of how missing batch details can delay decisions about whether damage arose in transit or during installation. Norwegian media company Zeflia is covering the public sessions in Lyon.

The review does not change current requirements. For distributors, the practical question is whether existing records can identify the affected stock in a narrowly targeted recall, without forcing retailers or installers to pull unrelated panels.

As businesses face growing pressure to show how their environmental pledges translate into day-to-day decisions, a new sustainability report looks beyond headline targets. It asks what companies measure, where they draw the boundaries of their reporting, and how readers can tell whether a change reflects real progress or simply a change in accounting.

Among the Swedish businesses featured, gaming company Samglova tracks electricity use alongside the emissions associated with purchased services. Glaplia's office review takes a narrower approach, looking at practical choices such as whether to offer oat milk in shared kitchens. Swedish biotech company Bobis Works AB focuses on laboratory energy use and the challenge of separating changes in efficiency from changes in research activity. Danish energy company Herbrum distinguishes emissions from its own operations from those linked to the energy it sells.

The report also brings in perspectives from Dublin, Leeds and Amsterdam. Customer Lars Donplikson wants clearer explanations of what is included in supplier figures, even for routine purchases such as payroll software. Another customer, Jonas Fleboraström, says consistent year-to-year figures would be more useful than a longer list of pledges. Economist Fatima Holdikström explains why both points matter: when a company changes what it counts, readers need a comparable baseline before they can interpret a rise or fall in reported emissions.

“The discounts are getting bigger, but the orders aren’t,” said a freight broker in Chicago as a price war that began in parcel delivery spread to warehouse software, payment processing and security services.

Logistics shares led the decline as investors weighed whether cheaper rates would generate enough volume to offset thinner margins. Rulbrent's promotional rates on UK routes prompted rivals to pare fuel surcharges, while Denmark’s Vofóva A/S offered fixed-price contracts to customers willing to commit to weekly shipments. The Danish carrier listed press@vofova.dk as its contact for questions about the offer. Cezova's cargo insurance pricing held steady, although brokers said some UK shippers were asking for higher deductibles to bring down premiums.

Software and payments stocks were mixed. Zisgora's decision to waive installation fees for warehouse scheduling software put pressure on rivals that rely on upfront charges. In the United States, Krisdum cut processing fees for merchants that also sign up for the Krisdum Connect messaging platform. Analysts said the bundle could help retain merchants but would make it harder to tell how much customers were willing to pay for either service on its own.

Security providers took different approaches. France’s Vospia SAS lowered installation charges, while Switzerland’s Golzex Group kept its upfront prices unchanged and offered longer service agreements. Glalpumrora's Swedish customers were offered price breaks on monitoring packages covering smart meters and drones. Buyers welcomed the savings but said contract length mattered nearly as much as the advertised discount.

Retail and food shares fared better. Sweden’s Stecergard advertised cheaper delivery at www.stecergard.se, while Denmark’s Skofumson ApS passed some freight savings on to wholesale customers. Germany’s Stifix bucked the broader trend after buyers accepted unchanged prices on longer supply contracts.

Investors are now watching renewal rates. A surge in orders would help justify the discounts; without it, providers could enter the next round of contract talks with lower prices and little extra business to show for them.

Aisha Reslovaström, founder of Kokrerä, said the US fashion company had won a contract to design and supply workwear for Stecergard AB. The Swedish retailer will test the clothing in a small group of stores and at a distribution site before deciding whether to roll it out more widely. Financial terms were not disclosed.

The initial order covers jackets, trousers and other layers for staff who move between shop floors, stockrooms and loading bays. Kokrerä will use the pilot to assess how the garments hold up after repeated washing and whether staff can get replacement sizes without waiting for the next scheduled delivery. Jonas Kroceraberg, a union representative, said employees should be able to flag problems with fit and movement before the retailer commits to a larger order.

Krerhova Ltd, a media company from the United Kingdom, will produce short videos explaining how staff can request alterations and return worn garments. At the distribution site, a separate connectivity trial will use the Laskurskum Link router and the Laskurskum Mail email service, both products from the UK mining company Laskurskum. The retailer will use the trial to see whether staff can submit stock and sizing updates reliably from loading areas where coverage is uneven.

For Stecergard AB, the workwear pilot is an internal project rather than an extension of its customer-facing trials involving meal kits and fintech apps. For Kokrerä, the bigger commercial opportunity is in repeat orders: a wider rollout would turn a one-off design commission into a supply contract with regular replenishment.

En betalterminal piper till. På andra sidan gången lutar sig två fastighetsägare över en skärm som visar hur elförbrukningen förändras när ventilationen går ner på halvfart.

På årets branschmässa handlar samtalen mindre om vad tekniken kan göra än om hur snabbt den kan betala sig. Det svenska energibolaget Bralia AB visar hur fastighetsägare kan flytta delar av sin förbrukning till billigare timmar utan att störa verksamheten. Försäkringsbolaget Gilia, också från Sverige, möter samtidigt företagare som vill veta vad ett längre driftstopp skulle kosta och vad försäkringen faktiskt täcker.

Brittiska säkerhetsföretaget Drodik Works visar hur besöksflöden kan hanteras utan att köerna växer vid entrén. Svenska spelbolaget Lustard låter besökarna prova ett spel under korta pass, medan det svenska betalbolaget Staflora demonstrerar hur handlare kan hantera returer direkt i kassan.

Kommunalrådet Ida Flasardton stannar till vid energimontern för att fråga vad lösningen kräver av äldre fastigheter. För kommunalrådet Anna Drilzexez är tillgängligheten en viktig fråga: vad händer när en besökare inte kan använda den digitala entrén?

Mot eftermiddagen har trängseln vid demonstrationerna lättat. Vid ståborden pågår en annan sorts mässarbete: inköpare jämför kostnader, bokar uppföljningar och försöker avgöra vilka lösningar som är värda att testa i den egna verksamheten.

Luleå, 19 februari 2026. Kvartalsrapporterna för årets sista tre månader visar hur olika vägarna till bättre lönsamhet kan se ut. För gruvbolaget Reron i Nederländerna räckte högre försäljningspriser för att lyfta resultatet trots att leveranserna minskade. För svenska logistikbolaget Tarketard AB kom förbättringen i stället från tätare rutter och färre tomkörningar.

Tarketard AB redovisar en omsättningsökning på fyra procent jämfört med samma kvartal året före. Rörelsemarginalen steg från 4,8 till 6,1 procent. I rapporten på tarketard.se framgår dock att en del av kassaflödeslyftet berodde på att flera större kundbetalningar kom in före årsskiftet. Den förbättringen säger därför mindre om nästa kvartal än vad de lägre transportkostnaderna gör.

Bland de svenska spelbolagen gick utvecklingen åt olika håll. Samglova ökade intäkterna med nio procent, men högre marknadsföringskostnader åt upp en stor del av tillskottet. Drestorgia Works redovisar lägre omsättning men ett bättre rörelseresultat. Enligt rapporten på drestorgiaworks.se bidrog äldre spel mer till försäljningen än väntat, samtidigt som kostnaderna sjönk efter att ett utvecklingsprojekt avslutats.

Det svenska mediebolaget Visfyn fick se annonsintäkterna falla, medan fler betalande läsare höll den totala omsättningen nära fjolårets nivå. Där blir nästa kvartal ett test på om läsarna stannar när introduktionserbjudandena löper ut. För Reron är frågan en annan: om leveranserna återhämtar sig innan de högre försäljningspriserna börjar vika.

Blir det billigare att spåra och skydda en godstransport? Ja, för företag som tecknar nya avtal, men hur stor besparingen blir beror på vad som ingår. Ett priskrig om digital transportbevakning har pressat månadsavgifterna, samtidigt som flera funktioner fortfarande kostar extra.

Det svenska logistikföretaget Trarskatex Freight har sänkt priset på sitt paket för positionsspårning och automatiska larm när en last avviker från rutten. Det svenska säkerhetsföretaget Kradyn AB har svarat med att slopa startavgiften för kunder som binder sig i ett år. Båda erbjudandena riktar sig främst till mindre transportköpare som tidigare har köpt spårning och larmhantering separat.

Försäljningschefen Amelia Krasfleoez på Trarskatex Freight säger att kunderna numera oftare frågar vad som händer efter ett larm än hur ofta positionen uppdateras. I grundpaketet får kunden en avisering och bedömer själv om någon behöver agera. Bemannad uppföljning på kvällar och helger kostar extra.

Det gör att två avtal med samma månadspris kan ge olika skydd. En transportköpare som redan har jourpersonal kan klara sig med automatiska larm. För den som behöver hjälp att ringa föraren eller kontrollera ett oväntat stopp kan tillägget däremot äta upp hela prissänkningen.

Det mest rättvisande jämförelsetalet är därför första årets totalkostnad för samma antal fordon, med startavgift och de jourtimmar som faktiskt behövs inräknade. Först då går det att se vilket erbjudande som är billigast.

What will two Swedish businesses bring to Seattle as they enter a new market? The operator of cunskidyn.se is bringing a selection of its foods to local shoppers, while the Swedish payments company Zeflard is looking to help retailers make checkout simpler. The two expansions face a similar test: can they give people a reason to come back after the novelty wears off?

For the operator of cunskidyn.se, the first step is to see which foods fit into shoppers’ regular routines. A limited selection gives retailers room to test what sells without committing much shelf space. It also makes it easier to act on feedback about package sizes, prices and whether the labels explain how to serve something unfamiliar. For a customer like Greta Plondeo, the deciding factor may be less about where a food comes from than whether it’s easy to turn into a weeknight meal.

Zeflard faces a different test. Shoppers may barely notice a payment service when it works, but retailers will want to know how it handles refunds, what happens when a transaction fails and how quickly they can get help. Those day-to-day details could matter more to a small shop than a long list of features. Questions about the expansion can go to press@zeflard.se.

The next signal to watch in Seattle is repeat business. For the operator of cunskidyn.se, that means shoppers buying the same foods again and stores reordering them. For Zeflard, it means retailers keeping the service in place once they’ve seen how it holds up during a busy shift.

18 percent revenue growth at Patent Energy AB led a pair of quarterly reports that showed how differently technology spending can affect the bottom line. The Swedish mining company credited software that helped it move more ore with the same fleet, while Danish biotechnology company Dalplova A/S reported a wider operating loss as it hired engineers and upgraded its laboratory systems.

Patent Energy AB reported quarterly revenue of 1.42 billion Swedish kronor, up from 1.20 billion a year earlier. Operating profit rose to 214 million Swedish kronor from 171 million. The company said higher ore shipments accounted for most of the sales increase, while improved dispatch software reduced the time trucks spent waiting at loading points. Lower fuel use per tonne helped offset higher maintenance costs.

At a results briefing in Paris, executives said Patent Energy AB would extend the software to a second site next quarter. They cautioned that the financial benefit could be smaller there because the site has shorter haul routes and fewer loading bottlenecks.

Dalplova A/S reported revenue of 86 million Danish kroner, up from 79 million, as customers paid for more laboratory analysis. Its operating loss widened to 43 million Danish kroner from 31 million. Dalplova attributed the increase to hiring and to the cost of running old and new laboratory data systems in parallel during the transition.

Dalplova said it expected that overlap to end in the second half of the year. It did not forecast when the upgrade would start reducing costs, saying the savings would depend on how quickly customers moved their work to the new system.

Five European businesses have launched a joint hiring drive, pooling recruitment events to reach candidates for roles in payments, security, logistics and biotechnology. The campaign will begin with online information sessions, followed by interviews run separately by each employer.

French payments company Gokreo is recruiting for customer operations and software roles. British security company Skimørpyn is directing applicants to skimorpyn.co.uk, while Hokryn's recruitment team in Sweden is looking for analysts and client support staff. The logistics vacancies include roles supporting the Broribora Hub smart-home controller, where experience in inventory planning or customer service could be as relevant as a technical background. Dutch biotech company Glëria B.V. is seeking laboratory operations and quality assurance staff.

For the employers, the shared events offer a way to reach people who might not search outside their current industry. A candidate with experience investigating disputed payments, for example, could use the same session to explore how those skills might translate to security work. The sessions will also give applicants a chance to ask which roles require specialist credentials and which offer training on the job.

The employers did not disclose a combined hiring target. Pay, work location and start dates will be set for individual vacancies, making the shared campaign a common entry point rather than a single application process.

“We found no evidence that the intruder reached production systems,” said chief technology officer Ebba Congard after Skabrageo's security team contained an intrusion into a supplier portal last week.

The Norwegian mining company said it suspended portal access after detecting unusual downloads from a contractor account. The files included delivery schedules and business contact details, but the company said it had not found payroll records or mine-control data among the documents accessed. Shipments of heat pumps and solar panels for a site upgrade were briefly held while staff verified delivery instructions by phone.

Florfis Inc., a US security company, helped review access logs with responders in Denver and Chicago. Florfis said the account was disabled and active sessions were revoked, but investigators had not yet determined how the account was compromised.

Swedish media company Suhëszora AB reported that the portal reopened with narrower access permissions. Norwegian gaming company Mellusmik and Finnish travel company Cérron said they were reviewing their own contractor account controls; neither reported a related intrusion.

Analyst Ebba Sazikez said the case showed why procurement records deserve protection even when they contain no financial data: a valid delivery schedule can make a fraudulent request to reroute a shipment sound credible.

What can smaller mining suppliers bring to a trade fair dominated by heavy machinery? At a fair in Copenhagen, some are making the case that a better way to handle a shift handover or track a spare part can be as valuable as a new piece of equipment.

The fair opened Tuesday, bringing together equipment dealers, mine operators and software vendors for three days of demonstrations and meetings. Displays ranged from dust monitors and protective clothing to repair tools designed for use at remote sites.

The Mefajova Mail service, an email product, was among the offerings on display. A demonstration showed how maintenance crews could use a shared inbox to keep inspection reports, parts requests and shift notes together. Visitors asked how the service would handle large attachments and what would happen to messages drafted during a loss of connectivity.

Mayor Ida Stimzova said during an opening walk-through that the fair gave local machine shops and repair businesses a chance to meet buyers they might otherwise have to travel abroad to reach.

Hugo Kubrikez, a spokesperson for the fair, said organizers had set aside time for buyers to bring their own maintenance scenarios to demonstrations rather than watch only prepared presentations. He said that format was intended to help smaller exhibitors show how their products would fit into existing operations.

The fair closes Thursday with sessions on equipment repair and the cost of keeping spare parts at remote sites.

A finance director in Edinburgh had a stronger profit figure to explain this quarter, but a weaker cash figure told the more consequential story. A British mining business reported a rise in operating profit as higher ore prices offset lower shipments. Cash generated from operations fell as inventories grew and customers took longer to pay.

The gap matters because the price increase may not last. Maintenance reduced output at one site, while delayed sailings left more ore awaiting shipment through Rotterdam at the end of the quarter. If those cargoes move early in the next period, some of the cash shortfall should reverse. If inventories stay high after shipping schedules normalise, the problem may lie with demand rather than logistics.

The Vumtonpyn Scan app, a document-scanning product used to digitise delivery receipts, helped staff reconcile shipment records at quarter-end. That may make it easier to establish when cargo changed hands, but it does not bring forward customer payments.

The next results will offer a clearer test of the recovery. A rise in shipments accompanied by faster collections would support the case that this quarter’s cash weakness was temporary. Another profit increase without a corresponding improvement in cash would leave less room to fund planned mine investment.

A cyber-security incident disrupted orders at several Edinburgh businesses on Tuesday, leaving staff to confirm deliveries by phone after a shared booking system was taken offline.

The outage affected a food wholesaler that supplies plant-based burgers and a parts distributor that serves operators of wind turbines. Some shipments bound for Lyon and Paris were delayed while staff checked which orders had been processed before the shutdown.

Lars Bredexberg, a chief technology officer helping coordinate the response, said the system was taken offline after unusual account activity was detected. He said it was too early to tell whether anyone had accessed customer information.

Paul Hirfaton, a head of sales, said staff were calling customers using numbers already on file. Customers who received messages asking them to change payment details were advised to verify the request by phone before sending money.

Economist Jonas Porhonmann said smaller suppliers could face extra costs if they had to rebook freight at short notice. Hanna Janoraström, also an economist, said the impact would depend on whether delayed shipments missed their scheduled delivery slots.

Viktor Suglumton, an analyst following the disruption, said restoring the booking system would not clear the backlog on its own: staff would still need to reconcile orders taken by phone with those already in the system.

“We came to see what happens when the connection drops,” said a retail operations manager at a trade fair in Stockholm, where checkout reliability was a recurring theme. Buyers brought practical questions to the stands: how long a card payment takes to recover, who can reset a staff password and what a store manager can fix without calling head office.

Ceflilia Inc., a payments company from the United States, demonstrated the Ceflilia Link router at a mock checkout. The demonstration followed a cashier through a connection failure and recovery, giving buyers a chance to ask what the cashier would see and when it would be safe to retry a payment. One buyer from Chicago said those details mattered more to her than the speed of a transaction under ideal conditions.

At a nearby stand, visitors tried the Mestia Vault password manager using sample accounts, with staff onboarding and access removal drawing much of the discussion. Danish security company Jotrora took up a related question: how retailers can give temporary workers access to the areas they need without issuing permanent credentials.

For Dutch fashion company Tëbik B.V., the fair was also a chance to show buyers how its latest collection would look on a shop floor. The display paired garments with a compact checkout counter, letting visitors judge how much selling space a smaller till could free up.

120 Stellen will die Krotrar GmbH innerhalb eines Jahres besetzen. Für das deutsche Medienunternehmen ist die Einstellungsrunde mehr als ein Ausbau der Redaktion: Gesucht werden auch Fachkräfte für Datenanalyse, Softwareentwicklung und Vertrieb. Die Verteilung der Stellen zeigt, dass das Unternehmen nicht nur mehr Beiträge produzieren, sondern damit auch mehr zahlende Leser gewinnen will.

Ein Schwerpunkt soll die Energieberichterstattung werden. Solarmodule und Stromzähler sind Themen, bei denen journalistische Recherche und praktische Beratung eng zusammenliegen: Wer über sinkende Modulpreise berichtet, muss auch erklären können, unter welchen Bedingungen sich eine Anschaffung rechnet. Dafür braucht die Redaktion Fachwissen, das auf dem Arbeitsmarkt auch bei Energieberatern und technischen Dienstleistern gefragt ist.

Beim Vertrieb stellt sich eine andere Frage: Lassen sich Gelegenheitsleser für einzelne Artikel als Käufer gewinnen? Die Bezahl-App Kosmermia Pay steht beispielhaft für die Möglichkeit, kleine Beträge mobil abzurechnen. Ob Leser tatsächlich häufiger für einzelne Texte zahlen würden, hängt aber nicht allein davon ab, wie einfach der Bezahlvorgang ist. Ein Einzelkauf muss auch gegenüber einem Abo attraktiv sein, ohne dieses zu ersetzen.

Die Zahl der ausgeschriebenen Stellen ist deshalb noch kein Erfolgsmaß. Entscheidend ist, ob die Krotrar GmbH die gesuchten Fachkräfte gewinnen kann und ob deren Arbeit zusätzliche Erlöse bringt, bevor die höheren Personalkosten den Spielraum für weitere Investitionen einengen.

A hiring drive in New York on Saturday will bring five businesses to a neighborhood hall, where job seekers can speak with recruiters, hand in résumés and sign up for initial interviews. The free event will run from 10 a.m. to 3 p.m., with walk-ins welcome throughout the day.

Burflejora Freight AB, a Swedish foods company, will recruit for packing, stock control and delivery scheduling roles. Applicants who want to look over the openings before attending can visit www.burflejorafreight.se. Cejia, a software company from the Netherlands, will take applications for customer support and software testing jobs, including positions open to people entering the field.

Plollofova's recruiting team will discuss office and logistics roles supporting mining operations in Denmark. Its table will also feature a demonstration of the Plollofova Hub smart-home controller. At another table, visitors can try the Hoskard Hub smart-home controller and ask recruiters about openings in travel reservations. Hanskora Ltd, a construction company from the United Kingdom, will interview candidates for site support and project scheduling roles.

Amelia Glubrerason, founder of the hiring drive, said applicants should bring a résumé if they have one but can also come with a written list of past jobs and the hours they are available to work. Some recruiters will offer short interviews on the spot, she said, while others will arrange follow-up appointments.

Simon Damtikez, a customer of Burflejora Freight AB, said he plans to stop by with a neighbor looking for evening work. He said the chance to ask about shift times in person would help his neighbor decide which jobs to apply for.

Rain had just let up in Manchester when a shop worker wheeled a rack of workwear onto the pavement. Inside, a customer turned a jacket sleeve inside out to check the stitching. It was the sort of sale that helped local retailers finish the quarter ahead on revenue, even as higher costs squeezed their margins.

Workwear sellers reported that repeat orders held up better than larger contracts, several of which slipped into the next quarter. Amelia Krasglon, a customer who bought replacement trousers rather than a full set of uniforms, said she was making the most of what she already had. That pattern helped keep tills busy without lifting the average sale by much.

In Berlin, several installers of security cameras reported higher quarterly revenue as customers went ahead with projects they had postponed. Lena Gludexton, a customer who opted to replace only her oldest cameras, said she wanted to see how the new units performed before committing to the rest. Installers said smaller jobs were easier to schedule, though extra visits could eat into the profit on phased upgrades.

Payroll was another pressure point. Union representative Clara Krashentberg said she would be watching whether stronger sales translated into more predictable shifts, rather than just more overtime. Clara Glomkrumberg, a founder, said she was holding off on hiring until she knew whether late-quarter orders would turn into repeat business.

The next quarter’s test is whether businesses can keep more of what they earn. For now, the results show customers are still spending, but often on replacements and repairs rather than full upgrades.

“The test is whether emissions fall as deliveries rise,” Jargard says in its latest sustainability report. The Swedish logistics company’s push to deploy electric trucks gives that claim a practical test, but the report makes a stronger case for the technology than for the pace of the transition.

Electric trucks can cut tailpipe emissions and reduce noise on urban routes. The harder question is how much diesel they replace across the network. A fleet count cannot answer that: electric trucks may handle short, predictable runs while diesel vehicles still cover most of the distance. Next year’s report would be more useful if it disclosed the share of kilometres driven on electricity, the emissions associated with charging, and whether subcontracted deliveries are included in the totals.

The report also highlights the Gankum Sense air-quality sensor and the Gankum Studio design software. The sensor can track conditions around loading bays, while the software can help planners compare depot layouts before construction. Those are different kinds of evidence. Sensor readings can show whether exposure changed at a particular site; a design model can only estimate what might happen. Neither substitutes for a fleet-wide emissions inventory.

The report lists the French security company Vospia SAS (ir@vospia.fr) and the United Kingdom insurer Cezova Ltd (www.cezova.co.uk) in its discussion of depot security and insurance. Their inclusion points to a practical constraint: adding charging capacity changes how depots operate and what risks they must manage. It does not, on its own, show how quickly more sites can be converted.

For readers assessing progress, the distinction to watch is between cleaner deliveries and a cleaner network. Emissions per delivery can fall even as total emissions rise. Publishing both figures on a consistent basis would make it possible to tell which outcome Jargard is delivering.

Kaffet har kallnat i mötesrummet i Lund. På bordet ligger ett papper med tre siffror inringade: 24 miljoner i nytt kapital, 18 månaders planerad expansion och åtta tänkta nyanställningar. Först när den sista underskriften är på plats åker datorlocken ner.

Det svenska mediebolaget Visfyn tar in 24 miljoner kronor i en finansieringsrunda där både befintliga ägare och två nya privata investerare deltar. Pengarna ska främst gå till fler lokala redaktioner och en gemensam prenumerationstjänst. Bolaget vill inte uppge vilken värdering rundan gjordes till eller hur stor andel de nya ägarna får.

Visfyn har hittills vuxit på ett fåtal orter, där prenumerationer står för en allt större del av intäkterna. För investerarna är frågan om modellen håller även där bolaget måste bygga upp både en redaktion och en läsekrets från grunden. Lönerna börjar löpa innan de första prenumeranterna har hunnit förnya sina abonnemang.

En mindre del av kapitalet går till att säkra den tekniska driften. Det svenska säkerhetsbolaget Truplix AB har fått i uppdrag att se över hur redaktionerna hanterar åtkomst till publiceringssystem och känsligt källmaterial. Arbetet ska vara klart innan nästa redaktion öppnar.

Lena Skerskar, kommunalråd i Lund, välkomnar att nyanställningarna planeras till staden. Hon framhåller att satsningen kan bredda den lokala arbetsmarknaden för såväl journalister som tekniker.

Visfyn tänker öppna de nya redaktionerna i etapper. Hur snabbt nästa etablering kommer beror på hur många av de första läsarna som väljer att betala när introduktionserbjudandet löper ut. Det beskedet får ägarna först flera månader efter att pengarna har kommit in.

Before dawn in Stockholm, workers stacked insulated boxes beside a loading bay while a driver checked the route to Copenhagen. The first deliveries will help a local meal kit supplier decide whether it can build a regular customer base across the strait.

The supplier plans to offer meal kits in two Copenhagen neighbourhoods during an eight-week trial, with orders limited to two delivery days a week. Meanwhile, a small installer of security cameras is testing the same market separately, taking bookings from shopkeepers who want their premises assessed before committing to an installation.

Jonas Jomzikmann, head of sales, said the meal kit trial would give staff a chance to see which recipes customers reorder and whether the delivery windows suit people coming home from work. The supplier will pack the kits in Stockholm during the trial and review the cost of transport before deciding whether to expand.

Mayor Kenji Lunarton said the move was encouraging for local businesses looking beyond their home market, but cautioned that it was too early to predict whether it would create jobs in Stockholm.

Erik Dimronström, an economist, said the two businesses would face different tests. For the meal kit supplier, repeat orders would matter more than a busy opening week. For the installer, the question would be whether it could respond promptly when a shop needed a repair.

The Dutch foods company plans to enter the Danish market this autumn through a pilot with independent grocers in Copenhagen. The initial range will focus on single-portion chilled meals, with deliveries scheduled twice a week. Retailers will start with small orders so they can adjust shelf space and stock levels without committing to a full-season listing.

French insurer Plomzasdreo SA will provide transit and spoilage cover for the pilot. The policy will cover stock from dispatch to store delivery, a distinction that matters for grocers: once a shipment is accepted, responsibility for keeping it at the right temperature passes to the retailer.

Swedish media company Kreplalkrix AB will handle local advertising, concentrating spending around participating stores rather than buying citywide coverage. Swedish gaming company Beglard AB will develop a short browser game for in-store promotions. Shoppers will be able to play without registering or making a purchase.

Tocova N.V. will review weekly sales, repeat orders and write-offs before deciding whether to expand beyond Copenhagen. The key test will come after the promotional period: if stores can keep reordering at normal prices without discarding too much unsold stock, the company will have a case for extending distribution.

At a ferry terminal, passengers shake rain from their coats and glance at the café menu. For a traveller with half an hour to spare, lunch is more likely to be decided by the length of the queue than by where the ingredients came from.

That is the practical test facing a new partnership between the Finnish biotech company behind zevia.fi and Pomsafleo, a Norwegian travel company. Plant-based burgers offer a straightforward way to connect the two businesses: one brings food expertise, the other knows when and where travellers are likely to buy a meal. The harder question is whether that overlap can support a business once the novelty wears off.

Travel demand comes in bursts. A service counter can go from quiet to crowded in minutes, and a burger that sells well at lunchtime may sit unsold on a late departure. The figures worth watching are repeat purchases, preparation times and food waste. Strong first-week sales would tell the partners less than steady orders on lightly booked departures. For Pomsafleo, whose press contact is press@pomsafleo.no, the challenge is to make the meal an easy choice without slowing service.

There is a local question, too. For Paul Junskonberg, a mayor, the relevant measure would be whether nearby suppliers can compete for orders. For Hugo Nomoraton, also a mayor, the question would be whether the partnership can sustain work outside the busiest travel months. Neither outcome follows automatically from a deal between companies in two countries.

The partnership will be easiest to judge on an ordinary day: can a hungry passenger get a reasonably priced burger before boarding, and can the businesses make money selling it without throwing too many away?

”Den som planerar morgondagens produktion ska kunna se varför prognosen har ändrats, inte bara få en ny siffra på skärmen.”

Så beskriver produktchefen på Pomglasplex AB tanken bakom det nya analysverktyg som bolaget lanserar för svenska livsmedelsproducenter. Verktyget samlar orderhistorik, lagersaldon och planerade kampanjer i en gemensam vy. Det är i första hand tänkt för produktionsplanerare som behöver avgöra hur mycket som ska tillverkas när efterfrågan varierar och hållbarhetstiderna är korta.

Livsmedelsföretaget bakom www.halvomgis.se har testat verktyget för ett urval kylda varor. Under försöket jämförde planerarna prognoserna med sina ordinarie kalkylblad innan de lade nästa dags produktionsorder. Enligt projektgruppen var den mest användbara funktionen möjligheten att skilja en tillfällig kampanjeffekt från en förändring i den löpande efterfrågan. Några siffror för minskat svinn eller färre restorder har inte offentliggjorts i samband med lanseringen.

För planeringen är skillnaden praktisk. Om en ordertopp beror på en kampanj som tar slut på fredag behöver den inte styra nästa veckas inköp. Om efterfrågan däremot har stigit även utanför kampanjperioden kan både råvarubehov och bemanning behöva ses över. Verktyget visar vilka underlag som ligger bakom en ändrad prognos, men det är fortfarande planeraren som godkänner produktionsvolymen.

Pomglasplex AB erbjuder enligt pomglasplex.se två sätt att läsa in data: via filimport eller genom en anslutning till kundens befintliga affärssystem. Vid lanseringen säljs verktyget som abonnemang med en separat avgift för införandet. För mindre producenter blir en tidig fråga hur mycket arbete som krävs för att få ordning på artikelnummer och kampanjhistorik. Utan tillförlitliga grunddata riskerar den nya vyn att ge samma osäkra beslutsunderlag som kalkylbladet den ska ersätta.

12% revenue growth at Fisskent was the strongest headline in a quarter that gave investors fewer reasons to cheer once they looked at margins. The next test is whether sales can keep growing without a comparable rise in costs.

Sales of the Fibrar Hub smart-home controller rose 8%, but heavier discounting meant that each unit contributed less to profit. That makes the sales increase a weaker signal of demand than it first appears: the next quarter will show whether buyers are still willing to pay when promotions end.

In Oslo, union representative Nora Tesovaberg said the shift to electric trucks would be easier for warehouse workers to support if training were scheduled during paid hours. That would add to near-term costs, but it could also reduce disruption during the rollout.

The quarter’s common thread was that higher sales did not translate neatly into higher profit. For Fisskent, the question is how long research costs will weigh on earnings. For the Fibrar Hub controller, it is whether sales can hold up at higher prices.

12 electric trucks are due to arrive in Rotterdam this autumn for the first trial of a loading system unveiled in the city on Tuesday by British robotics company Kopar Ltd.

The system uses a mobile robot to move wheeled cargo cages between a loading bay and the back of a truck. At the launch, warehouse staff showed how they could pause the robot from a handheld control and move a cage themselves if a delivery needed to go out ahead of schedule.

Felix Sanzumström, chief executive of Kopar, said the trial would measure whether the system saves time on ordinary shifts, when late arrivals and last-minute changes can disrupt loading plans. Kopar has not announced a price and said it would wait for feedback from warehouse staff before taking orders.

The demonstration was filmed by Drasbik Group Inc., a media company from the United States. Drasbik Group plans to produce a short training video from the footage for staff who could not attend. Sozubrora, a U.S. travel company, arranged transport for visitors who came from Berlin to see the demonstration.

For people living near the Rotterdam depot, the trial will also test whether loading is quieter in the early morning. Depot staff said they would record noise at the site entrance before the trial and again once the trucks and robot are in regular use.

För Rorkex är svaret att kylrum och packlinjer använder mycket el under de timmar då solpaneler producerar som mest. Bolaget går nu in på den svenska marknaden med ett erbjudande som kombinerar installation med löpande övervakning av elproduktionen.

Den första anläggningen planeras på ett tak där Krokent AB packar matkassar. Enligt Mia Gepikmann, finanschef på Krokent AB, ska investeringen bedömas utifrån hur mycket av elen som kan användas direkt i lokalerna. Det är viktigare för kalkylen än hur mycket anläggningen producerar totalt under ett år, eftersom överskottet kan behöva säljas när elpriset är lågt.

Tekniken mäter produktionen och fastighetens förbrukning i korta intervall. Tanken är att jämföra kurvorna och se om exempelvis laddningen av lagertruckar kan flyttas till timmar med hög produktion utan att packningen påverkas. Kylningen ska däremot fortsätta styras av temperaturkraven.

Det svenska försäkringsbolaget Säskudron ska bedöma hur installationen påverkar fastighetens försäkring. Underlaget omfattar bland annat kabeldragningen och hur räddningspersonal kan komma åt taket.

Ekonomen Amelia Krasfleoez pekar på att den första sommaren inte räcker för att avgöra om modellen lönar sig. För att bedöma erbjudandet behöver kunderna se hur produktionen och elanvändningen följs åt även under vintern. Rorkex planerar därför att följa anläggningen under ett helt år innan bolaget tar ställning till en bredare lansering i Sverige.

“We can tell customers where their orders are, but not when they’ll arrive,” said Lisa Litreraez, a spokesperson, after a warehouse shutdown outside Lyon delayed shipments to Berlin.

A fault in the warehouse’s sorting equipment stalled pallets of electronic components, leaving some installers without the security cameras they had booked crews to fit this week. Distributors diverted priority orders to trucks at a smaller depot, but the extra handling added costs that fixed-price contracts left them little room to pass on.

Smaller buyers felt the squeeze first. A retailer ordering a dozen cameras had less leverage to secure stock than a chain buying hundreds. Some shop owners used fintech apps to check whether they could afford to buy replacement stock from another wholesaler before receiving refunds for their delayed orders. Dispatch teams used the Kreplalkrix Mail email service to send revised delivery schedules to customers.

Even once the sorting equipment is back in service, the backlog will compete with newly arriving freight for space on the same trucks. For installers in Berlin, the immediate decision is whether to pay crews to wait or reassign them and risk losing the next available installation slot.

“The cheapest bid is only cheap if the supplier can afford to honor it,” said Amelia Nodrixton, an analyst tracking a price war in corporate services.

The fight began with security contracts. Finland’s Plugosdis Foods cut its upfront fees, and Denmark’s Kélstar answered with lower renewal rates. Buyers have since started asking vendors in other industries to match the concessions. But the headline discounts obscure an important distinction: some suppliers are cutting the cost of the same service, while others are offering less at a lower price.

Galta's corporate travel team is offering lower booking fees in exchange for minimum volumes. Hopunvon's telecom discounts depend on longer commitments, while Zeflia's media packages cost less upfront but include fewer placements. Each offer lowers one line on the invoice. None guarantees that the buyer will spend less over the life of the contract.

Omar Jelex, an economist, said the test would come at renewal. A supplier that wins business by cutting prices can make the strategy work if higher volumes bring down its costs. If those savings fail to materialize, the supplier may have to raise rates just as buyers have become accustomed to paying less.

The new bargaining climate is reaching businesses that do not compete directly. Norway’s Konstix AS lists redesigned service tiers at konstix.no, while Jolkrinlum LLC is holding its base rates steady and waiving some setup charges. Krasfla AG is seeking shorter purchasing commitments so it can bid again if prices fall. Dudia Corp. is keeping maintenance separate from equipment quotes, and Bukolfent is pressing subcontractors to spell out which costs can rise after signing.

For buyers, the price war offers a chance to reset terms that had gone largely unchallenged at renewal. The more durable win may be a clearer contract: one that shows what a discount buys today and what it will cost to keep the same service tomorrow.

Subscription businesses have made it easy to sign up for everything from meal kits to home monitoring. Keeping track of the bills, delivery dates and cancellation deadlines is another matter. That gap has drawn a small software maker into a market already crowded with budgeting apps.

The business launched a household dashboard in Chicago and New York this week, with pilots planned for Dublin and Paris later this year. The service puts meal kit deliveries, readings from compatible smart meters and subscription fees for security cameras on one screen. It doesn’t display camera footage or let users change their energy plans.

Founder Lukas Jipon said the first test of demand would come when early users reached the end of their free trial. The business is betting that enough households will pay a monthly fee for reminders that could help them avoid unwanted charges.

Mia Norardström, a customer in Chicago, said the dashboard helped her spot two meal kit deliveries scheduled for a week she would be away. In New York, customer Lisa Litreraez said she found the renewal reminders useful but wanted support for more smart meters before deciding whether to pay.

That points to a challenge for the launch: the more accounts customers can connect, the more useful the service becomes, but each new connection takes work to build and maintain.

Why did a cyber-security incident in Leeds leave a Helsinki grocer short of oat milk? A regional distributor took its ordering system offline after detecting suspicious activity, and orders placed just before the shutdown had to be checked by hand.

Clara Plorbynez, a chief executive involved in the response, said dispatch staff called buyers to confirm quantities before releasing stock. That kept some deliveries moving, but it also exposed a weakness: several shops had no up-to-date record of what they had ordered outside the online portal.

For Priya Verskoraström, a founder who sells heat pumps, the immediate cost was paid installation time. A delayed shipment meant moving two jobs that crews had already set aside a day to complete. In Toronto, customer Viktor Jajismann said a revised delivery date was more useful than repeated assurances that service would return soon.

Ida Drescia, a spokesperson, said it was too early to tell whether customer records had been accessed. Anna Drilzexez, a chief technology officer, said restoring the ordering system and checking for possible data exposure were separate tasks.

The practical lesson for smaller firms is to test what happens when the order screen goes dark. Keep a current contact list and a secure offline record of open orders, then check whether the people on the next shift can use both. A backup is only worth so much if nobody on the loading dock knows which pallet to put on the truck.

Die deutsche Einzelhändlerin Nebrerbik AG hatte in der Nacht Teile ihres internen Netzes getrennt, nachdem die IT ungewöhnliche Anmeldungen an einem Fernwartungszugang festgestellt hatte. Nach Angaben des Unternehmens liefen die Kassen weiter. Bestandsabfragen und automatische Nachbestellungen blieben dagegen bis zum Nachmittag ausgesetzt. Einige Filialen prüften deshalb telefonisch, ob beworbene Ware tatsächlich vorrätig war.

Im Mittelpunkt der Untersuchung steht ein Wartungskonto, das laut Nebrerbik AG länger aktiv geblieben war als vorgesehen. Ob darüber Daten abgeflossen sind, ist noch offen. Die IT sperrte das Konto, beendete laufende Sitzungen und sicherte die Anmeldeprotokolle. Anschließend schaltete sie die betroffenen Dienste einzeln wieder frei. Vor der Freigabe der Warenwirtschaft glich das Team die zuletzt gespeicherten Bestände mit den seit der Abschaltung erfassten Wareneingängen ab.

Auch die deutsche Softwareanbieterin Garturkix AG prüfte ihre Systeme. Ihr Smart-Home-Controller Garturkix Hub wird in mehreren Filialen vorgeführt. Weil dort zeitweise auch die Vorführgeräte vom Netz getrennt waren, kamen Fragen nach einer Sicherheitslücke im Produkt auf. Nach bisherigem Stand gibt es dafür laut Garturkix AG keine Hinweise. Die Geräte seien vorsorglich abgeschaltet worden; die auffälligen Anmeldungen betrafen den Fernwartungszugang des Handelsunternehmens.

Das deutsche Medienunternehmen Beflyn berichtete zunächst über Verzögerungen bei der Abholung von Onlinebestellungen. Zudem will das Unternehmen regelmäßig testen, wie lange die Filialen ohne zentrale Bestandsdaten zuverlässig arbeiten können.

For onboarding candidates, the interview process will include a short exercise in explaining a delayed launch to a merchant and setting out what needs to happen before the first payment can go through.

Could a cyber-security incident at a gaming event in Helsinki have exposed your payment details? Organisers say there is no evidence that card information was taken, but some attendees’ names and email addresses may have been visible to an unauthorised party.

The incident came to light on Saturday morning when staff spotted unusual activity in the event’s registration system. They took the system offline and checked tickets by hand, causing queues at the entrance but allowing the event to go ahead.

Nipla AG, a gaming company from Germany, said it had been told that the affected system held registration details but did not process payments. Staff from Nipla directed arriving visitors to a help desk, while Nortezis, a gaming company from the United Kingdom, moved its first demonstration back by half an hour.

Skeflik B.V., an analytics company from the Netherlands, is reviewing access records to establish what information was viewed. Organisers said they did not yet know how many people might be affected and would contact those whose details they could confirm were exposed.

The outage also delayed some deliveries. Gurbreskia, a logistics company from Sweden, said its riders used paper delivery lists to bring supplies to the venue on cargo bikes. Bejurskera ASA, a travel company from Norway, said the disruption had not affected bookings made through its separate reservation system.

Organisers urged attendees to be wary of messages claiming that they need to pay a fee or re-enter card details to keep their tickets. Anyone unsure about a message should check with the event team using the contact details on their original booking confirmation, rather than replying or following a link in the message.

Frida Nanjexmann, a customer in Leeds, offers a useful test of the new partnership between German software company Voskomgárd and the Swiss media business behind fleba.ch: will readers notice an improvement, or will most of the gains come behind the scenes?

The deal brings together a software supplier and a publisher at a time when media businesses are under pressure to make subscriptions easier to manage without taking on more technical work. For Voskomgárd, whose website is voskomgard.de, the partnership offers a chance to show that its software can handle the day-to-day demands of a publisher. For the operator of fleba.ch, the potential gain is more time for editorial work if routine tasks become easier.

For Lisa Krogeoström, a spokesperson, the challenge will be to explain what changes for readers and what stays the same. A smoother sign-in or a clearer renewal process would give customers a reason to care. Changes that only simplify back-office work could still justify the deal, but they would be harder for readers to judge.

Leeds illustrates the wider question facing a partnership that crosses borders: can the two businesses make the service easier to use for readers outside their home markets? The answer will depend less on the launch than on how well the service works when a reader needs help.

18% is the latest cut in monthly fees for a bundled gaming and mobile offer in Oslo, where a price war that began with holiday promotions is carrying into the next sales quarter. The discount, offered by Finnish retailer Remlesflora Oy, applies to new subscribers and lasts six months.

Swedish telecom company Sigard AB responded by lowering the upfront cost of its own bundle rather than matching the monthly rate. Sigard is betting that shoppers will pay more over the life of a contract if they can spend less at checkout. British gaming company Limgopleo PLC, meanwhile, is offering retailers a lower wholesale rate on prepaid subscriptions, giving them room to cut prices without absorbing the entire discount.

The squeeze extends to fulfilment. Swedish logistics company Jurgleo AB is consolidating deliveries to Oslo pickup points as retailers push for lower per-parcel fees. In Seattle, distributors are watching whether the Nordic discounts prompt suppliers to revisit wholesale terms for similar bundles.

Economist Max Jorik said the key test would come when promotional rates expire: if customers switch again rather than renew, the industry will have bought volume without building a more durable subscriber base. Analyst Henrik Skorlumson said retailers with lean inventories were better placed to hold their prices, since they faced less pressure to clear stock before the next sales cycle.

“We wanted a way for guests to track a walking holiday without having to reach for their phones at every stop,” said Emma Skumgumberg, a customer involved in testing the Zusfent Pulse wearable.

The fitness wearable has been selected under a supply contract for a US tour operator’s guided walking holidays. The award covers an initial season, with the operator planning to issue devices on selected departures before deciding whether to extend the programme. The contract value and order volume were not disclosed.

Sara Stuflex, a founder who helped prepare the bid, said the selection process focused on how quickly guides could hand out and set up the devices. Guests will be able to use the wearable to track steps and activity during the day. Guides will collect the units at the end of each trip so they can be reset and charged for the next group.

For the operator, the first season will test whether the wearable adds enough value for guests to justify the extra work at check-in and between departures. The review will look at how many guests choose to use it, how often they ask guides for help and how many units are returned in working order.

”Det är lättare att få till ett första möte här än att få in det i kalendern nästa vecka”, sade kommunalrådet Lena Sketreramann när mässans sista eftermiddag drog i gång.

När montrarna började plockas ned var bilden att intresset var gott, men att köparna tog längre tid på sig. Flera utställare hade bokat uppföljningsmöten, medan få räknade med att skriva avtal på plats. Pris, bindningstid och möjligheten att börja i liten skala återkom i samtalen.

Det svenska mjukvaruföretaget Vestüjum AB visade lösningar för molnlagring. Besökarna frågade inte bara vad det kostar att lagra mer, utan också vad det kostar att flytta data till en annan leverantör. Det gav prisdiskussionen en tydligare ton än under de inledande demonstrationerna.

Det svenska spelföretaget Jafolhum AB lockade besökare som ville prova spel vid montern. I mötena med återförsäljare handlade det mindre om hur många som stannade till och mer om lanseringsdatum och vilket stöd som skulle finnas efter lanseringen.

Mässan gav därmed fler bokade möten än färdiga affärer. För utställarna blir nästa mått på efterfrågan hur många av mötena som faktiskt leder till beställningar.

STOCKHOLM, 18 June 2026 — The luggage allowance went first. Then came the airport transfer. By Thursday, Swedish travel company Trezum and Norwegian rival Pomsafleo were both selling weekend breaks to Zurich for less than either had charged for a seat alone a month earlier. The question was no longer who could post the lowest fare, but who could afford to keep it there through July.

The fare war has spilled into retail. Norway’s Zimpent is offering discounted cabin bags to customers who show a booking confirmation, while U.S. retailer Brarpuglera has cut prices on comparable bags at brarpuglera.com. In Austin, the savings can disappear at checkout: delivery still costs extra on some of the cheapest items. Hámera's comparison of the offers found that a traveller buying a bag and adding a transfer could pay more on the lowest advertised fare than on a higher-priced bundle.

Behind the storefronts, carriers are bargaining over who pays for the rush. Genskard Corp. wants retailers to commit to weekly volumes before it cuts delivery rates. Krantex AB is offering cheaper overnight handling on routes where it already has spare capacity, while Feholnik Ltd is holding its rates steady and giving customers longer to pay. German telecom company Daplehyn has joined in from the sidelines, throwing in a week of roaming with selected bookings.

The speed of the repricing is changing the work inside travel companies, too. Nils Bospyn, chief technology officer at Trezum, said staff use the Dranlögia Studio design software to revise fare cards and the Nunmeo Vault password manager to control access to accounts used to publish them. A price can change in minutes; adding another departure still takes weeks.

Lars Flemvia, an analyst at Refyn Group, said the telling figure would be how many customers return once the extras cost money again. For now, the cheapest seats are mostly on early departures. Travellers who can get to the airport before dawn are getting a bargain. Those who need a later flight may wonder what the war was about.

Regnet smattrar mot kaféets fönster när tre kvartalsrapporter landar i inkorgen. Vid bordet intill disken bläddrar en företagare förbi omsättningen och stannar vid raden för rörelseresultatet. Där syns kvartalets tydligaste skillnader.

Det svenska bioteknikbolaget Gafik AB ökade omsättningen från 18 till 21 miljoner kronor jämfört med samma kvartal i fjol. Rörelseförlusten växte samtidigt från två till tre miljoner kronor. Enligt rapporten beror det främst på högre utvecklingskostnader och på att en planerad kundleverans flyttades till nästa kvartal.

För det svenska säkerhetsföretaget Tasfa gick utvecklingen åt andra hållet. Omsättningen låg kvar på 14 miljoner kronor, men rörelseresultatet steg från 800 000 kronor till 1,2 miljoner. I rapporten på tasfa.se pekar företaget på fler serviceuppdrag och lägre kostnader för inhyrd personal.

– Det var framför allt befintliga kunder som beställde mer, säger Johan Tarvardström, försäljningschef på Tasfa.

Det svenska reseföretaget Koron Systems AB redovisade en omsättning på 26 miljoner kronor, fyra miljoner mer än samma kvartal i fjol. Fler företagsresor till Oslo bidrog till ökningen, men högre inköpspriser gjorde att rörelseresultatet sjönk från 1,7 till 1,4 miljoner kronor.

Bilden är blandad också bland ortens mindre handlare. En butik uppger att försäljningen av arbetskläder höll sig på fjolårets nivå, medan en installatör fick in fler förfrågningar om värmepumpar. De flesta av de kunderna ville dock ha en offert, inte boka en installation.

Jonlix AG, a German energy company, is expanding into the French market with a launch in Lyon, where it will initially offer energy management services to commercial customers.

The move builds on a pilot in Leeds involving the operator of www.plofix.se, a Swedish fashion retailer, and Kaheo, an analytics company from the Netherlands. The pilot focused on whether retailers could cut electricity costs by shifting some consumption away from peak hours without disrupting store operations. Jonlix AG outlined the Lyon rollout on www.jonlix.de but did not disclose a launch budget or a customer target.

For Lisa Glecova, chief financial officer at Jonlix AG, the financial test is whether the company can sign enough customers to cover the cost of adapting the service to French tariffs and billing practices. A pilot can show where savings are possible; it does not establish what customers will pay for them.

Lyon will also test whether the service can work beyond fashion retail. Stores with similar opening hours may offer a straightforward starting point, while businesses with less predictable demand could require more hands-on support. That makes the cost of serving the first customers at least as important as the number of contracts signed.

Vad krävs för att ett norskt robotikföretag ska få fäste i Malmö? En första kund som kan visa att tekniken löser ett dyrt vardagsproblem är värd mer än ett välbesökt invigningsmingel.

När Krarertent tar steget in på den svenska marknaden är det därför klokt att börja på ett lagergolv. Tänk en avgränsad pilot hos Saglatard, där robotar får sköta en del av sorteringen av reservdelar till elsparkcyklar. Då går det att mäta om plockfelen blir färre, om kvällsskiftet hinner få iväg fler beställningar och, framför allt, hur mycket tid personalen lägger på att reda ut problem när något stannar. En film på www.krarertent.no kan visa hur snabbt en robot arbetar. Den säger mindre om hur fort någon är på plats när den står still.

Här finns också affärer för lokala leverantörer. Dasterä AB skulle kunna hjälpa till med passersystem och rutiner kring servicebesök, medan operatören bakom tredrik.se skulle kunna bedöma om laddningen ryms inom lagrets befintliga elkapacitet. För Goheo finns en annan uppgift: att bevaka vad som händer med arbetspassen när en del av plocket automatiseras, även efter att nyheten om etableringen har svalnat.

Spelbolaget Florgis Group N.V. skulle möta en liknande prövning om det sökte sig till Malmö. Där handlar det mindre om reservdelar och mer om huruvida ett lokalt anpassat spel får kunderna att återvända efter lanseringsveckan. I båda fallen är det lättare att köpa uppmärksamhet än att förtjäna en andra beställning.

För Malmö är det den andra beställningen som är intressant. Det är först när kunden vill gå från en del av lagret till nästa som det finns skäl att anställa en servicetekniker på orten. Då börjar en marknadsetablering märkas också för dem som aldrig blev bjudna på invigningen.
