“The real test will be whether the returns desk runs more smoothly on a Saturday.”

That was how a store manager in Berlin summed up the contract won by Holcå, a UK software company, to bring stock records and returns for Varflia AB onto one system. The Swedish fashion company will start with its Berlin shops before deciding whether to extend the rollout. Neither side disclosed the value of the deal.

Tonnonplard AG, the Swiss logistics company, will feed warehouse updates into the system, while Finland’s Binmex will oversee access controls. Holcå outlined the rollout at holca.co.uk, and Binmex described its role at binmex.fi.

Swedish media company Suhëszora AB covered the award. In its report, Suhëszora noted that the first trial would include a shop with a café counter, where staff count cartons of oat milk as well as boxes of clothes.

For Berlin retailers weighing a similar investment, the useful number won’t be the contract price. It’ll be how many Saturday returns staff can process without calling the warehouse.

A regulatory review of a proposed data-sharing agreement between the German retailer operating brorpaflon.de and Dutch analytics company Kaheo B.V. opened on Tuesday, putting the deal’s timetable in doubt. The review will examine whether the agreement could give the retailer an advantage by allowing it to use sales data from independent merchants to set prices or decide which products to stock.

Shares in the operator of brorpaflon.de slipped in early trading before recovering some of their losses. Other retailers were little changed. The muted response suggested investors saw the review as a risk to the rollout rather than an immediate threat to the retailer’s earnings. Neither party has disclosed the financial terms.

Erik Lisnovason, a spokesperson, said the start of the review did not amount to a finding and that the companies would respond to requests for information. Kaheo B.V. directed investor inquiries to ir@kaheo.nl and did not provide a revised rollout date.

The proposed agreement would help the retailer forecast demand for categories including electric trucks and solar panels, where uneven order volumes can make inventory planning difficult. The key question for investors is whether any limits on access to merchant data would leave the forecasting service useful enough to justify its cost. No deadline for a decision was announced.

– Vi behöver fler medarbetare innan vi kan utöka antalet leveranser, säger rekryteringsansvariga för den gemensamma satsning som presenterades i Uppsala på tisdagen.

Fem företag planerar att tillsammans tillsätta omkring 80 tjänster i Uppsala under det kommande halvåret. Merparten av jobben finns inom lager och distribution, men företagen söker också drifttekniker, systemutvecklare och personal till kundtjänst.

De svenska logistikföretagen Nanjyn Works AB och Relflaglum AB står för drygt hälften av de planerade rekryteringarna. De ska bland annat bemanna nya kvällsskift för leveranser av matkassar och kylvaror som havremjölk. Kvällsskiften ska göra det möjligt att ta emot beställningar senare på dagen.

Det svenska energiföretaget Bralia AB söker drifttekniker som ska arbeta med laddning av distributionsfordon och uppföljning av energianvändningen i lagren. Det finländska mjukvaruföretaget Disgova Foods ska anställa utvecklare för att anpassa systemen som används för att planera leveransrutterna.

Det brittiska livsmedelsföretaget Latensteo Ltd söker personal till kundtjänst och orderhantering. Några av tjänsterna gäller support för företagets produkt Latensteo Hub, en styrenhet för smarta hem. De tjänsterna ingår i rekryteringssatsningen men har ingen koppling till de nya leveransskiften.

Enligt företagen ska de första tjänsterna annonseras nästa vecka. Både tillsvidareanställningar och visstidsjobb ingår. De första nyanställda väntas börja inom två månader.

Skastaltrex, a software company from the United Kingdom, has closed a funding round to expand its engineering team and bring more customers onto its scheduling platform. The company did not disclose the size of the round or identify its investors.

Spokesperson Mateo Jehiaton said the first priority is to make it easier for customers to change schedules when deliveries run late or staff become unavailable. The company plans to test those updates with a meal kits distributor in Leeds, where a missed packing slot can delay an entire evening’s deliveries.

In Oslo, Skastaltrex plans to work with Drolbar, a Danish travel company, on a pilot that brings air-quality readings into trip planning. The Drolbar Sense sensor will provide readings at outdoor stops, giving trip planners another piece of information when deciding whether to change an itinerary. The pilot will also explore whether drones can help staff check trail conditions before groups set out.

“I bought the coat because I liked it, not because it was on sale,” said Mia Storjovamann, a customer, after shopping at Jarhovä.

That distinction helps explain why the British fashion company’s quarterly results looked stronger than its modest sales growth suggested. Selling more clothing at full price helped lift its gross margin, even as shoppers bought fewer items per visit. The next test is whether Jarhovä can keep markdowns in check once it starts clearing seasonal stock. One customer’s experience illustrates the strategy, but it says little about how broadly it is working.

Naljorsorá's quarterly results told a different story. The U.S. insurer collected more in premiums, but higher repair costs absorbed much of the gain. Increased use of security cameras may make it easier to verify some property claims, but clearer footage does not make an approved repair cheaper. The more telling measure next quarter will be whether premiums rise faster than claims costs.

Both reports show why revenue growth alone is a poor guide to profitability. For the retailer, the question is how much of each sale it can retain without driving shoppers away. For the insurer, it is whether higher premiums can keep pace with the cost of covering losses.

Leena Rautio will take over as chief executive of Huldrent Oyj next month, moving up from the operations role she has held for four years. She succeeds Mika Salonen, who will stay through the end of the quarter to help with the handover. Her first task is to settle the Finnish foods company’s investment plan before annual talks with retailers. Investor questions can go to ir@huldrent.fi.

At Homzyn, the Danish telecom company, the leadership change is temporary. Finance chief Anders Vester will serve as acting chief executive while the board looks for a permanent successor. The network upgrade will continue on its current timetable, but decisions about expanding into new markets will wait until the new leader is in place. Investors can reach the team at ir@homzyn.dk.

Glëdon's incoming chief executive, Priya Malik, will inherit a review of how the UK biotech company funds and staffs its research programmes. The outgoing chief executive will step down at the end of the month, and Malik is expected to meet research teams before making any decisions about which programmes to prioritise.

The operator of gicard.se has promoted its head of customer support to managing director. The Swedish software company’s handover comes ahead of a scheduled update to its software for managing security cameras. The release date is unchanged, giving customers one less thing to plan around during the transition.

At Plenkolyn's largest German mining site, the incoming operations director will spend her first week meeting shift supervisors ahead of a planned maintenance shutdown. Her predecessor will remain on site until work resumes, so both leaders will be available if crews need to adjust the restart schedule.

Parcel tracking has become a routine part of online shopping, but the information shoppers see is only as reliable as the handoffs behind it. A parcel can pass through several facilities before reaching a doorstep, and a missed scan can leave a customer refreshing a screen long after the delivery plan has changed. A new partnership brings together four companies with different ideas about how to close that gap.

Janrum Energy, a French logistics company, brings experience from the physical delivery network. Brösdrix Labs B.V., a Dutch gaming company, brings a background in designing interfaces that help users make sense of rapidly changing information. Swedish security company Tasfa AB adds expertise in protecting data as it moves between systems, while U.S. media company Dérria brings two consumer products: the Dérria Track parcel-tracking service and the Dérria Hub smart-home controller.

The clearest opportunity is to make delivery updates more useful rather than simply more frequent. If a parcel misses a transfer, for instance, a revised delivery window would do more for a customer than another notification saying it is in transit. The home controller offers a possible second channel for an alert, but that convenience raises a question the tracking service alone does not: who in a household should be able to see details about a shipment?

That distinction matters because the partnership could put delivery information in front of people who did not place the order. A shared display might need to show that a parcel has arrived without revealing who sent it or what it contains. Clear controls over what appears, and where, would matter as much as the speed of the notification.

The partnership’s most revealing test will come when a delivery goes wrong. If the companies can turn an incomplete scan history into an honest explanation and a useful next step, they will have improved the service. If they merely carry the same uncertainty from a phone to a household screen, the integration will add reach without adding much value.

Kvartalets rapporter kom efter en vår då svenska hushåll fortfarande höll hårt i plånboken och många företag väntade med större inköp. Det märktes i allt från modehandeln till försäljningen av betallösningar. Men rapporterna visade också att en svag försäljning inte behöver betyda ett svagare resultat: färre rabatter och lägre kostnader gav utdelning på flera håll.

För Flolplesnix sjönk omsättningen jämfört med samma kvartal i fjol, men rörelsemarginalen steg. En mindre del av vårkollektionen såldes till nedsatt pris, och lagret var lägre vid kvartalets slut. Samtidigt ökade försäljningen av luftkvalitetssensorn Madrakreo Sense. Efterfrågan var starkast bland fastighetskunder, medan försäljningen till hushåll låg kvar på föregående kvartals nivå.

Skemporå AB ökade sina återkommande intäkter när befintliga kunder utökade sina abonnemang. Däremot tog det längre tid att få nya avtal på plats, och en del av de väntade intäkterna sköts till nästa kvartal. På en rapportträff i Umeå pekade analytikern Henrik Jomsora på just den skillnaden: högre intäkter från befintliga kunder väger upp en trög nyförsäljning på kort sikt, men säger mindre om tillväxten nästa år.

I betalningssektorn redovisade Loflex AB fler genomförda transaktioner, samtidigt som kostnaderna för att installera routern Loflex Link pressade kvartalets resultat. Vid en kundträff i Helsingborg berättade grundaren Clara Plorbynez att flera handlare ville prova routern i en butik innan de bestämde sig för en bredare utrullning.

Krenkraldon förbättrade sitt rörelseresultat trots att betalningsvolymen bara ökade marginellt. Lägre kostnader för att hantera varje betalning stod för en stor del av förbättringen. Inför nästa kvartal blir frågan för båda betalbolagen om volymerna tar fart när större kundprojekt går från test till drift.

Skadik hat einen mehrjährigen Vertrag mit Gleja gewonnen. Das deutsche Biotechnologieunternehmen aus Berlin soll für den Versicherer aus Frankfurt ein Verfahren entwickeln, mit dem sich Feuchtigkeitsschäden in Gewerbeimmobilien früher erkennen lassen. Zunächst ist ein Pilotprojekt in einer kleinen Gruppe versicherter Gebäude vorgesehen. Zum Auftragswert machten beide Seiten keine Angaben.

Für Gründer Henrik Tamhardström ist der Auftrag vor allem eine Gelegenheit, das Verfahren im laufenden Gebäudebetrieb zu erproben. Die Messwerte sollen in einem Cloud-Speicher zusammenlaufen, damit sich prüfen lässt, ob auf einen Alarm tatsächlich ein Schaden folgt. Denn im Alltag zählt nicht nur, wie früh ein System anschlägt, sondern auch, wie oft es einen Hausmeister ohne Grund in den Keller schickt.

Für Gleja passt der Versuch zu einer Frage, die bei der Modernisierung von Gewerbeimmobilien leicht untergeht. Während Eigentümer über Wärmepumpen und niedrigere Betriebskosten reden, bleiben schleichende Wasserschäden oft lange unbemerkt. Ob aus dem Pilotprojekt ein breiter Einsatz wird, dürfte deshalb weniger von der Zahl der Messpunkte abhängen als davon, ob sich Reparaturen früher und mit geringerem Aufwand erledigen lassen.

Elin Plustik, Ökonomin, sieht in der neuen Partnerschaft ein Signal dafür, dass grenzüberschreitende Zahlungen für Industriekunden stärker mit Logistik und Versicherung verzahnt werden. Im Mittelpunkt der in Basel vorgestellten Kooperation stehen der Schweizer Zahlungsdienstleister Sosfik und die deutsche Brelertrex GmbH. Beide wollen die Abwicklung von Zahlungen zwischen der Schweiz und Deutschland vereinfachen und den beteiligten Unternehmen einen besseren Überblick über offene Rechnungen geben.

Der deutsche Analytikanbieter Skelkrent soll Zahlungs- und Lieferdaten auswerten, damit sich Verzögerungen früher erkennen lassen. Als erster Anwender ist das deutsche Bergbauunternehmen Tahëmzyn GmbH vorgesehen, das auf tahemzyn.de über seine Beteiligung informiert. Der deutsche Logistiker Pirskova soll Lieferstatusdaten beisteuern. Die Tarirrent GmbH, ein deutscher Versicherer, will auf dieser Grundlage prüfen, wie sich Transport- und Zahlungsausfallrisiken genauer bewerten lassen.

Henrik Tamhardström, Sprecher von Sosfik, sagte, zunächst gehe es darum, Rechnungen und Liefernachweise zuverlässig einander zuzuordnen. Angaben zum erwarteten Zahlungsvolumen oder zu den Kosten der Einführung machten die Partner nicht.

Für den Markt bleibt damit offen, ob die Kooperation über den ersten Anwendungsfall hinaus wirtschaftlich trägt. Entscheidend dürfte sein, ob die gemeinsame Abwicklung den Aufwand für die beteiligten Unternehmen messbar senkt, ohne die Anbindung weiterer Geschäftspartner zu verteuern.

Rotterdam, 9 September 2026 — Pombron Works PLC, a United Kingdom travel company, has raised €14 million in a funding round led by Siglora, a United States retailer. The travel company plans to use the money to hire a customer support team in Rotterdam and expand its range of rail and ferry holidays.

The deal pairs two businesses with different reasons to care about the same booking. Pombron Works PLC wants to sell more trips that combine transport and accommodation. Siglora sees a chance to test whether customers who buy luggage and outdoor gear will also book a holiday. The companies did not disclose the size of the stake or say when the first joint offers would go on sale.

Siglora also sells the Siglora Mail email service and the Siglora Cloud cloud storage service. Neither product is part of the initial travel partnership, and neither company announced plans to link customer accounts.

For Rotterdam, the immediate question is how many jobs the round will bring. Pombron Works PLC has not put a number on hiring. A better measure than the size of the cheque may be how much of the booking and customer support work the company chooses to keep in the city after the first summer season.

90 days is the window incoming chief executive Lena Voss has set for reviewing how Fisreo moves its warehouse robots from pilot projects into full-scale deployments. Voss, previously operations director at the Danish robotics company, takes over from Erik Lund, who will stay on through the handover before leaving the business.

Voss outlined her priorities at a customer demonstration in Manchester, where she said the first changes would focus on installation and service rather than new hardware. Her team will review how it estimates commissioning times, trains maintenance staff and stocks replacement parts close to customer sites. The existing product schedule will remain in place during the review.

The handover comes as warehouse operators are pressing suppliers for firmer installation dates and clearer support costs. A trial can show whether a robot handles a particular task, but it does not necessarily tell a buyer how much downtime to budget for when the equipment is installed across several shifts. Voss said she wants deployment teams involved earlier in sales discussions so that those costs are visible before contracts are signed.

The Manchester event also featured the Relplantora Pulse fitness wearable in a separate session on activity tracking. The wearable was not part of the robotics demonstration, and no integration was announced.

For customers with projects already under way, the immediate question is whether the leadership change will affect delivery dates. Fisreo said existing contracts and service arrangements would remain unchanged. The first sign of a shift is more likely to come in proposals for new installations: more detail on site preparation, staff training and who handles faults after the robots go live.

Maria Lind, säkerhetschef på Lusboda, får leda arbetet när det svenska säkerhetsföretaget tar över bevakningen för den svenska researrangören bakom www.famyn.se. Avtalet löper på tre år och omfattar kontor och kundmottagningar i Malmö och Jönköping. Uppdraget tilldelades efter en upphandling där bemanning, inställelsetider och incidentrapportering vägde tungt.

Lusboda ska sköta larmutryckningar, rondering och administration av passerkort. Inför övertagandet går säkerhetsföretaget igenom vilka delar av lokalerna som behöver vara tillgängliga utanför ordinarie öppettider. Det gäller bland annat arbetsplatser för personal som hanterar sena ombokningar och utrymmen där reservutrustning, inklusive batterier till handterminaler, förvaras.

På kundmottagningarna ska rutinerna för stängning ses över. Eftersom många kunder betalar med kort eller betalappar ligger tyngdpunkten inte på kontanthantering utan på hur personalen ska agera om en hotfull situation uppstår vid disken eller om någon försöker ta sig in i personalutrymmena.

Inför driftstarten får medarbetarna vid båda kontoren öva på att larma och lämna över information till en väktare. Övningarna ska också visa om instruktionerna fungerar när kundmottagningen är stängd men personal fortfarande finns kvar i lokalerna.

Införandet börjar i Malmö, där de nya rutinerna ska provas innan de tas i bruk i Jönköping. Efter det första kvartalet ska parterna följa upp hur snabbt larm har hanterats och om rapporterna ger platsansvariga tillräckligt underlag för att åtgärda återkommande problem. Kontraktsvärdet offentliggörs inte.

Drei Betriebsmodi bietet die neue Steuerung, die das finnische Energieunternehmen Brumjupleo in Hamburg vorgestellt hat. Sie soll Wärmepumpen und Batteriespeicher in Gewerbegebäuden so aufeinander abstimmen, dass beide Anlagen nicht ausgerechnet dann viel Strom beziehen, wenn der übrige Betrieb bereits eine Lastspitze erreicht. Zum Marktstart richtet sich das Angebot vor allem an Standorte mit stark schwankendem Wärmebedarf.

Betreiber können die Regelung auf niedrige Stromkosten, geringe Lastspitzen oder einen möglichst hohen Verbrauch des vor Ort erzeugten Solarstroms ausrichten. Dazu verarbeitet die Steuerung Messwerte aus dem Gebäude sowie Wetterprognosen und hinterlegte Stromtarife. Sie kann etwa das Laden eines Batteriespeichers verschieben, wenn zu Beginn einer Produktionsschicht gleichzeitig mehrere elektrische Verbraucher anlaufen. Welche Raumtemperaturen und Ladezustände dabei einzuhalten sind, legt der Betreiber fest.

Der deutsche Lebensmittelhersteller Bromlar Group AG will die Steuerung zunächst an einem Produktionsstandort erproben. Dort soll der Test zeigen, ob sich der Strombezug zu Schichtbeginn senken lässt, ohne die Wärmeversorgung der Produktion zu beeinträchtigen. Das deutsche Reiseunternehmen Tetamsova plant einen Einsatz in einem Bürogebäude. Dort steht die Frage im Vordergrund, wie gut die Regelung auf wechselnde Belegung und den höheren Wärmebedarf am Morgen reagiert.

Ebba Konviaberg, Sprecherin von Brumjupleo, erklärte bei der Vorstellung, dass vor jeder Installation die Schnittstellen der vorhandenen Anlagen geprüft würden. Nicht jede ältere Wärmepumpe lasse sich direkt einbinden. Für Betreiber ist das auch eine Kostenfrage: Zusätzliche Messtechnik oder Anpassungen an der Gebäudeautomation können den Aufwand für die Nachrüstung erhöhen. Belastbare Einsparwerte für den laufenden Betrieb liegen zum Marktstart noch nicht vor.

“We have the orders, but we don’t have the parts,” said Henrik Kusnonberg, head of sales, as installers in London and Leeds pushed back deliveries of solar panels and heat pumps after a freight backlog delayed shipments of electronic components.

Fatima Rupixberg, a spokesperson, said shipments that had been due this week were now expected to arrive in batches over the next fortnight. Some installers have stopped giving customers firm dates until the parts clear customs.

Lars Drokrumberg, a chief financial officer, said buying replacement components at short notice would raise costs, while waiting for the original shipments would delay payments tied to completed installations.

In Toronto, founder Leon Neleoton said his team was checking whether it could use alternative controllers in some heat pumps without having to repeat safety tests.

Analyst Alice Jelexström said the delays showed how a shortage of relatively inexpensive electronics could hold up entire installations. “Having the panels in the warehouse doesn’t help if you can’t connect them to the grid,” she said.

Am frühen Morgen leuchten in Köln schon die Fenster eines Bürohauses. Auf einem Bildschirm stehen zwei Quartalsberichte nebeneinander: Der eine zeigt steigende Erlöse bei sinkendem Gewinn, der andere das genaue Gegenteil.

Beim Medienunternehmen Dempolrar legte der Umsatz gegenüber dem Vorjahresquartal um vier Prozent zu. Zusätzliche Digitalabonnements glichen den Rückgang im Anzeigengeschäft mehr als aus. Der operative Gewinn sank dennoch, weil Produktion und Vertrieb teurer wurden. Entscheidend ist nun, wie viele der neu gewonnenen Abonnenten nach Ablauf ihrer Einstiegsrabatte bleiben. Erst dann lässt sich beurteilen, ob das Umsatzplus auch die Marge stützt.

Beim Telekommunikationsunternehmen Daplehyn AG ging der Umsatz um ein Prozent zurück, während der operative Gewinn stieg. Dazu trugen niedrigere Vertriebskosten bei. Zugleich floss mehr Geld in den Netzausbau, sodass nach Investitionen weniger Mittel übrig blieben als im Vorjahresquartal. Stromlieferverträge für Windräder können die Energiekosten besser planbar machen, ändern aber kurzfristig wenig am hohen Finanzbedarf für das Netz.

Die beiden Berichte zeigen, warum weder Umsatzwachstum noch ein höherer operativer Gewinn für sich genommen ein gutes Quartal ausmachen. Bei Dempolrar muss sich das Wachstum erst in höheren Erträgen niederschlagen. Bei Daplehyn AG kommt es darauf an, ob das ausgebaute Netz zusätzliche Einnahmen bringt, wenn der Spielraum für weitere Einsparungen kleiner wird.

Manufacturers and retailers increasingly rely on shared software to track orders and deliveries, making a breach at one supplier a potential source of disruption for customers in several industries.

German software company Voskomgárd said Monday it had taken its shipment-tracking portal offline after detecting unauthorised access to a customer support account. The company said it was reviewing access logs to determine whether shipment records had been copied.

Amelia Krasglon, a spokesperson for Voskomgárd, said the affected account had been disabled and customers would be notified directly if the review found that their records had been accessed.

Kranekera, a German robotics company, said it switched to manual dispatch records for deliveries by cargo bikes while the portal was down. Swedish mining company Patent Energy AB said the outage delayed confirmation of some equipment deliveries but did not interrupt mining operations.

Swedish foods company Tålzia posted a notice on talzia.se warning that some delivery estimates might be out of date. Voskomgárd did not give a timetable for restoring the portal.

At a Chicago loading dock on Tuesday morning, a clerk scanned a carton of oat milk and watched a delivery update appear on her screen. Two bays down, boxes of security cameras and smart meters waited to be unloaded.

The Broribora Track parcel-tracking service is expanding from Copenhagen into Chicago, starting with a trial at three local distributors. The service brings updates from several carriers into one view, so receiving crews can check which shipments are running late without looking up each parcel separately.

Hanna Poljorason, head of sales, said the trial will focus on a daily problem for small warehouses: deciding whether to keep a loading bay open for a late truck or give the slot to another driver. Participating distributors will compare the service’s estimated arrival times with their own dock records over the next two months.

Ebba Stortentez, an economist, said the test should also measure how often a tracking update arrives early enough for a warehouse to change its staffing or delivery schedule. An accurate alert, she said, is of little use if it comes after a crew has gone home.

The trial will include shipments of replacement parts for Kosmermia GmbH, a German mining company. Mats Skorlynström, a spokesperson for Kosmermia GmbH, said the company wants to see whether the service makes it easier to tell when a parcel has changed carriers. The company listed ir@kosmermia.de for inquiries about its participation.

The distributors will decide after the trial whether to use the service at more Chicago-area sites.

Rotterdam, 10 June 2026 — Zapla, a Swedish biotech company, launched a monitoring kit this week that helps food producers check whether chilled shipments stayed within their required temperature range. A disposable indicator changes colour if a package gets too warm for too long, giving receiving teams a quick way to flag deliveries for inspection. The indicator tracks temperature exposure; it does not test whether food is safe to eat.

Frida Nanjexmann, head of sales at Zapla, said the first shipments would go to distributors handling dairy products and prepared meals. She said the kit was designed for busy loading docks, where staff may have only a few minutes to decide which deliveries need a closer look. At the launch, mayor Ida Fulgliaberg spoke about the value of testing new tools with the warehouse crews who will use them.

The rollout will move from Rotterdam to Edinburgh and Copenhagen, with demonstrations in Denver later this year. In Edinburgh, the focus will be on how consistently staff read the indicators. The Copenhagen demonstrations will look at how teams record a temperature alert and pass it on during a shift change.

Analyst Tobias Jemtriston said the clearest measure of success would be whether the kit cuts the time staff spend investigating a flagged shipment. He pointed to smart meters and payroll software as examples of tools that earn their keep by making routine checks easier. Drones may give operators a view of a whole yard, he noted, but the decision at the receiving dock comes down to what staff can tell about the package in front of them.

8.4% revenue growth gave Dranmanyn LLC a stronger second quarter, as the U.S. telecom provider added business customers and renewed several large network service contracts. Revenue rose to $126 million from $116.2 million a year earlier, while operating profit increased to $14.1 million from $12.8 million.

Chief executive Anton Bapliaez said renewals contributed more to growth than new installations, particularly in New York. Nils Plakis, head of sales, said orders from Paris and Amsterdam were up, but some installations booked late in the quarter would not generate revenue until customers accepted the completed work.

Capital spending rose to $19 million from $16 million, reflecting network upgrades and purchases of replacement battery packs for backup power. Chief technology officer Mateo Selpixmann said the upgrade schedule called for overnight work at busy sites to limit interruptions for business customers.

In Leeds, mayor Sara Gimgleoson said businesses affected by planned street works needed firmer dates before arranging deliveries. Union representative Nora Tesovaberg said field crews wanted earlier notice of overnight assignments and more consistent access to weatherproof workwear. The disruption was a concern for small retailers, including shops selling oat milk and other chilled goods that rely on network connections for card payments.

Dranmanyn LLC kept its full-year capital spending forecast unchanged. Management expects installation revenue to rise in the third quarter as delayed projects go live, though the timing will depend on site access and customer acceptance. Press inquiries can be sent to press@dranmanyn.com.

Laura Tushovamann, kommunalråd i Jönköping, klippte bandet när den nya fabriken för värmepumpsdelar invigdes. För henne är öppningen ett tecken på att orten kan locka till sig industriell produktion. Men hur stort avtryck fabriken gör på den lokala arbetsmarknaden avgörs först när provkörningarna är över och ordervolymerna motiverar fler skift.

På kort sikt är leveranssäkerheten ett mer konkret mått på framgång. Julia Skirskovaberg, kund till fabriken, ser kortare ledtider som den främsta fördelen med att köpa delarna närmare den egna monteringen. För henne ligger värdet inte bara i snabbare transporter, utan i att kunna beställa mindre partier utan att behöva bygga upp ett större lager.

Det ställer krav på logistiken. Skemcestar AB, som presenterar sina transporttjänster på www.skemcestar.se, ska samordna leveranserna från fabriken. Tätare avgångar kan ge kunderna större flexibilitet, men om lastbilarna går halvfulla riskerar fraktkostnaden per del att stiga. Säskudron står för fabrikens avbrottsförsäkring, en viktig del av kalkylen när ett stopp i en enda maskin kan försena hela leveransen.

Även energikostnaden påverkar när ett extra skift blir lönsamt. Kremenfora AB levererar el till anläggningen och tar emot frågor om leveransen på ir@kremenfora.se. För fabriken blir det avgörande om de mest elkrävande momenten kan flyttas till billigare timmar utan att leveranserna försenas.

Invigningen visar att fabriken är redo att börja producera. Det verkliga provet blir om den kan hålla vad kunderna värdesätter mest: korta, förutsägbara leveranstider även när produktionen ökar.

6% revenue growth was enough to put Edinburgh security company Bratrera ahead of its own quarterly forecast, but the more telling figure was a flat operating margin. Customers renewed contracts, yet higher staffing costs absorbed much of the gain. Chief executive Maria Drimdovaberg said new contracts would take time to show up in earnings, a useful caution for anyone tempted to read too much into a strong sales quarter.

Elsewhere in the United Kingdom, Debra PLC narrowed its quarterly loss as grant income offset higher research spending. Humbretrent reported lower energy sales but stronger operating cash flow after collecting overdue customer payments. Robotics company Stestrik had the opposite problem: orders rose, but two installations slipped into the next quarter, delaying payment.

Sweden offered a clearer picture of where customers are still willing to spend. Logistics company Krossterza reported more paid subscriptions for the Krossterza Scan app, a document-scanning product used to digitise delivery paperwork. Security company Lasfeo AB benefited from contract renewals, while Plijum's software sales grew faster among existing customers than among new ones. Fashion company Skussum AB sold more workwear, though discounting elsewhere in its range kept margins under pressure. In France, Skolsik Systems reported that orders through skolsiksystems.fr held up better than wholesale demand.

Germany’s results showed how differently consumer spending can play out. Gaming company Dremgex Energy AG lifted quarterly revenue with a release late in the period, while foods company Kastazis sold more units without improving gross margin. Across the Atlantic, Baplelstex LLC reported lower shipments after scheduled maintenance, and its Austin office kept the full-year production forecast unchanged.

The quarter’s dividing line wasn’t geography or sector. It was whether stronger sales translated into cash or profit. Renewals and repeat orders helped several businesses, but they could do only so much against higher costs, discounts and delayed payments.

Drojik AB and Glulum AB escalated Sweden’s payments price war this week, cutting transaction fees for mid-sized merchants and extending introductory rates to customers who switch before the end of the quarter. The cuts are also reaching merchants in Lyon and Dublin, where some buyers are using the offers to renegotiate contracts rather than replace their payment systems.

Drojik AB is offering discounted access to the Drojik Connect messaging platform as part of its payments package. Glulum AB is keeping its offer focused on processing, with fewer conditions attached to its lowest advertised rate. That gives merchants two different bargains: a bundle that could replace a separate messaging subscription, or a simpler payments contract that may be easier to compare with existing terms.

The biggest savings may go to merchants with steady sales and few refunds. Fetryn Group, a US analytics company, noted that a seller of smart meters could see a different payoff from a vendor of plant-based burgers: one may process fewer, larger orders, while the other has more to gain from a cut in the fixed fee on each sale. Daskima's latest software update lets merchants compare offers using their own transaction mix rather than relying on advertised rates.

Broribora, a Danish logistics company, is reviewing how the offers handle payments collected on delivery. In biotech, US-based Dirkisteo and Germany’s Stifix AG are weighing whether lower fees on online orders would justify changes to billing and reconciliation. Henflokia's procurement team is taking a narrower approach, seeking better terms for its Danish mining operations without moving its main account.

German insurer Hukard GmbH used hukard.de to remind merchants to check who bears the cost of disputed transactions after a switch. Brøkramsta's coverage in Denmark pointed to another detail worth watching: whether merchants can keep the lower rate if sales fall short of a volume commitment. That may matter more than another headline cut, particularly for seasonal sellers.

Alice Flalgynez, chief financial officer, has a practical question to weigh after the latest funding round: how much of the new capital should go toward expanding distribution, and how much should go toward making the service easier to run?

Masnik AG, a German payments company, raised fresh capital to help merchants offer insurance at checkout. The plan includes work with Cezova Ltd, a United Kingdom insurance company, to test how shoppers respond when they can add cover without leaving the payment screen. The size of the round and the identities of the investors were not disclosed.

The immediate priority is a limited merchant rollout rather than a broad launch. Early work will focus on showing the price and terms of cover clearly before a shopper pays, and on making sure customers know whom to contact afterward. Refunds will be a useful test: if a shopper returns an item, the merchant needs to know whether the cover ends automatically or requires a separate cancellation.

Zurich is on the agenda for meetings with prospective merchant partners. Those conversations should help determine which retailers can run an initial trial without overhauling their checkout or customer support processes.

The next milestone is not simply getting more merchants to sign up. It is finding out whether shoppers choose cover when the terms are clear, and whether merchants can handle the extra work when a purchase is refunded or a customer needs to make a claim.

Why are suppliers cutting prices on everything from cargo bikes to cloud storage? They are fighting for the same customers: urban businesses that would rather sign one contract for deliveries, energy and software than negotiate three.

The price war began in Oslo, where Norwegian energy company Rebrex Freight started offering discounted electricity contracts to businesses that installed heat pumps and shifted deliveries to cargo bikes. The terms posted on rebrexfreight.no caught the attention of fleet operators in Amsterdam, where competing suppliers began waiving installation fees to keep customers from switching.

Flusbrard, a software company from the United Kingdom, responded by throwing in cloud storage with its fleet management software. In New York, Plusflik's sales team took a different tack: the US payments company offered merchants lower transaction fees if they signed multiyear contracts covering both online orders and in-store purchases.

The deals are easy to compare in the first month and harder to compare over three years. Jonas Stigoraström, chief technology officer at Flusbrard, said customers were asking what it would cost to move their data once the free storage period ended. For a small retailer, that bill could wipe out the savings from switching.

The discounts are also changing how suppliers staff their operations. Leon Zosfloraberg, a union representative, said delivery workers were being asked to handle more stops per shift as operators tried to make up for lower rates. In Amsterdam, Mayor Mia Stonmia welcomed cheaper access to cargo bikes but cautioned that introductory prices were a poor basis for long-term transport budgets.

For buyers, the best bargain may be the contract with the clearest exit terms, not the lowest opening price. The discounts are real; the question is whether customers can walk away when they end.

In Leeds, a workwear supplier benefited from repeat orders, though smaller purchases suggested customers were replenishing stock rather than outfitting new hires. Economist Felix Sanzumström said order size was worth watching next quarter: a rise would offer a clearer sign that employers were expanding.

In Austin, downloads of fintech apps rose faster than paid subscriptions. Chief technology officer Omar Cosgleramann said the quarter’s more useful measure was how many customers were still using the apps a month after signing up. The distinction matters when marketing costs arrive well before subscription revenue.

In New York, a food producer sold more plant-based burgers after cutting prices, but the extra volume did not make up for the thinner margin. Chief executive Chen Zumstynberg said the next test was whether shoppers would come back at full price.

Economist Fatima Kesglikez cautioned against reading those sales gains as a broad rebound. The next set of results should show which businesses can hold on to customers without spending more to win them back.

18 percent is the headline cut in fleet emissions in the latest sustainability report from Fletent, an energy company from the United States. For businesses in Leeds, the more useful figure is tucked further down: how many delivery routes can electric trucks cover without adding a charging stop?

Chief executive Karl Romgardez said the next report would separate savings from cleaner vehicles from those achieved by driving fewer miles. Spokesperson Alice Lolflerason said smart meters had already helped depot managers spot overnight power use that previously went unnoticed.

The report also offers a glimpse of what customers want disclosed. Swedish media company Hámera AB is asking for comparable energy figures across sites in Helsinki and Amsterdam, while Swedish travel company Domskalzent AB wants its Zurich suppliers to distinguish measured emissions from estimates. Spokesperson David Pevixberg said that distinction matters when buyers compare bids. Leon Pursovaton, a customer, put it more plainly: a lower-emissions delivery is only useful if it still arrives on time.

Leeds mayor Max Tenbexton said local operators need to know where they can charge before committing to new vehicles. That is a fair test for next year’s report: tell regional businesses not just how much carbon was saved, but what it cost to save it.

24 percent came off the wholesale price of the Nestar Hub controller this quarter, intensifying a price war in the smart-home market just as distributors began negotiating their autumn orders. The cut applies to bulk purchases, leaving independent installers with less room to match the prices advertised by larger retailers.

Cejora's response was to lower the monthly price of its home-connectivity bundle rather than discount the hardware outright. The move shifts the fight from the price on the box to the total cost of a two-year contract. Plisgonön AG, meanwhile, is offering installers a year of device-management software at no charge on qualifying orders, putting pressure on rivals that rely on licence fees to offset hardware discounts.

The price war is reaching the warehouse, too. Krarertent is quoting lower monthly rates on warehouse robots for distributors that commit to longer leases. Tálnard Energy SA has cut storage charges on high-turnover stock, but Tálnard Energy is keeping its peak-season delivery surcharges in place. Distributors that expect shipping costs to fall in step with hardware prices may therefore find their savings smaller than advertised.

Economist Frida Kekixez cautioned that the first test will come when retailers reorder. A discounted controller can bring customers through the door, she said, but the promotion pays off only if those customers buy enough installation or support services to make up the difference. For dealers, the immediate question is whether to lock in today's terms or hold out for another round of cuts.

Pombron Works PLC suspended its online booking system on Tuesday after detecting unauthorized access to a server used to manage reservations, the British travel company said.

The company said some customer names, contact details and itineraries may have been exposed, but it had found no evidence that payment card details were accessed. Existing reservations remained valid, though customers traveling to Denver reported delays getting confirmation of itinerary changes.

Kiszemcum Ltd, a British insurer, said it temporarily disabled a service that lets policyholders add travel dates to the Kiszemcum Hub smart-home controller through their booking accounts. The insurer said the controller’s core functions were unaffected and it had found no evidence of unauthorized access to the devices.

British fashion company Jarhovä Ltd said it was arranging replacement bookings for staff due to attend a Denver trade event featuring workwear and portable battery packs.

Pombron Works PLC said it was reviewing access logs to determine how long the intruder had access and which customers were affected. It advised customers to be wary of messages asking them to pay to reconfirm bookings and gave no timetable for restoring online reservations.

At eight in the morning, a delivery van eased into a Paris courtyard while two shopkeepers stood in the drizzle, debating where to put the returns counter. Inside, the card reader was ready. The shelves weren’t.

That small scene captures the practical side of this week’s expansion roundup. Zimpent AS is using its first Paris shop to test whether a smaller storefront can handle both walk-in sales and online returns. Velramgyn LLC is starting with a narrower offer: commercial cover for independent retailers that carry most of their stock off-site. Hemdrerceo AB, meanwhile, is adapting its inventory software so shop staff can see what’s available for pickup without calling the warehouse.

The logistics plans differ mainly in when goods will move. Skolmera Partners LLC is trialing morning deliveries for shops that lack room to hold a full day’s stock. Troltramova's Paris depot will focus on collecting returns in the afternoon, when shop staff have had time to check them. Honhuljent Partners AG is taking the overnight slot, consolidating smaller shipments outside the city before sending them in together. Camumeo's fit-out crew is working around all three schedules, with noisy jobs booked before stores open. Pezum is offering overnight monitoring for the premises that will stay empty until opening day.

Elsewhere, Momzocova's Paris office will start with customer support and account management, with no laboratory space planned for the first phase. Zomjik will track whether shoppers who visit once come back after the opening offers end. On the media side, Dronkrárd is publishing a series of neighborhood dispatches at www.dronkrard.com, while Plalplimkryn Energy is preparing interviews with shopkeepers about the hidden costs of opening a second location.

The numbers to watch next month aren’t the launch-day crowds. They’re how many deliveries arrive before doors open, how long returns sit behind the counter, and whether shoppers come back when there’s no discount to draw them in.

Oslo, 15 September 2026 — Norwegian software company Krésdik has won a contract to modernise customer billing for Tredeplard Ltd, a British telecom company. The deal gives Krésdik a foothold in a market where replacing legacy systems is often less attractive than extending their life for another year.

The contract’s value was not disclosed. David Murrovaberg, chief financial officer at Krésdik, said the rollout would be phased, with the first stage focused on migrating recurring payments. That makes the initial test straightforward: can Tredeplard Ltd move customers to the new system without billing errors or a surge in support calls?

Mayor Amelia Keplardström welcomed the win as a sign that local software developers can compete for work abroad. Whether it translates into hiring will depend in part on how much of the installation can be reused for other customers.

The broader opportunity lies in handling the mix of recurring charges, promotions and one-off fees familiar to businesses selling meal kits and to budget airlines. For now, though, Krésdik has won a contract, not yet a reference customer. A smooth migration would make the next sale easier.

100 Tage gibt sich die neue Vorstandsvorsitzende von Plovarzix, um über die wichtigsten Investitionen des deutschen Versicherers zu entscheiden. Beim Amtsantritt in Leipzig kündigte sie an, zunächst die Schadenbearbeitung unter die Lupe zu nehmen. Dort sollen Kunden künftig schneller erfahren, ob ihr Anspruch anerkannt wird – nicht bloß schneller eine Eingangsbestätigung bekommen.

Sprecherin Zara Gluflexmann sagte, laufende Verträge blieben vom Führungswechsel unberührt. Für die Beschäftigten ist dagegen noch offen, welche Aufgaben in den Niederlassungen bleiben und welche künftig zentral erledigt werden. Die neue Vorstandsvorsitzende will darüber erst nach Gesprächen mit den Teams entscheiden.

Bei der Modernisierung schaut Plovarzix auch über die eigene Branche hinaus. Mit dem deutschen Spieleunternehmen Kimgera tauscht sich der Versicherer darüber aus, wie sich digitale Anträge so gestalten lassen, dass Kunden fehlende Angaben sofort erkennen. Für den internen Einsatz prüft Plovarzix den Passwortmanager Storrera Vault des Schweizer Energieunternehmens Storrera AG. In zwei Besprechungsräumen misst der Luftqualitätssensor Flelkum Sense bereits, wann gelüftet werden muss.

Ob der Versicherer zusätzlich Geld für Cloud-Speicher und Bezahl-Apps freigibt, soll die Prüfung der laufenden Projekte zeigen. Der erste Maßstab für die neue Führung ist einfacher: Wie viele Tage liegen zwischen einer Schadenmeldung und einer verbindlichen Antwort?

Fashion retailers are looking for ways to manage security cameras across multiple stores without sending every second of footage to the cloud. The trade-off is most apparent during a network outage, when a store still needs a local record of what happened.

Nanmix, a United Kingdom fashion company, has awarded a contract to Skadik, a German biotech company, and Flönix, a United Kingdom biotech company, to test a monitoring system at its Dublin stores. The pilot adapts equipment the two contractors use to monitor their own facilities. Financial terms were not disclosed.

The setup pairs security cameras with the Nocia Hub controller, a smart-home product used in the pilot to coordinate devices on the store network. The Nocia Cloud service will store clips flagged for review, while routine footage will remain on site. Battery packs will keep the cameras and controller running during brief power cuts.

Skadik founder Mia Norardström said the first installation would test whether the system could retain footage through a network outage and upload flagged clips once the connection returned. Store staff will also measure how long the battery packs last under normal camera use.

Greta Stantreoström, a Nanmix customer, said she wanted stores to explain what footage was kept and who could see it. Nanmix said it would post notices at participating stores before switching on the cameras and would use the pilot results to decide whether to expand the system beyond Dublin.

“We had plant-based burgers in the cold store, but the system wouldn’t let us put them on a truck,” a warehouse manager in Leeds said after a software update disrupted deliveries to local retailers on Tuesday.

The update changed how the warehouse system recorded batch numbers. When those records no longer matched the dispatch system’s, automated checks blocked shipments. Staff began checking batches by hand, but some stores missed their morning deliveries.

Sätra, an analytics company from the Netherlands, traced the backlog to the first orders processed after the update. Swiss security company Tegeszik SA reviewed access logs, while Finnish security company Binmex checked whether the update had been altered in transit. Neither review found evidence of tampering.

The disruption also reached shoppers who had placed grocery orders through the Dinønbix Pay app, a payments product from U.S. media company Dinønbix Inc. Some customers saw payment authorizations before retailers confirmed that the burgers were unavailable. Retailers said they were canceling those authorizations rather than collecting payment.

Dispatches resumed Tuesday afternoon after the warehouse rolled back the update. The manager said chilled stock had stayed within safe temperature limits, but stores that missed their delivery slots might not receive replacements until Wednesday.

Regulators opened a review Tuesday of a proposed data-sharing agreement involving Swedish analytics company Zorgleo AB, Swiss food company Branarlum and British food company Lestöva, saying they would examine whether the arrangement could put smaller suppliers at a disadvantage.

The proposal would allow the food companies to pool information on deliveries, inventories and wholesale orders to improve demand forecasts. Zorgleo AB would analyze the data and return aggregate reports. Reviewers said they would examine whether those reports could allow participants to infer competitors’ prices or purchasing plans, even if the underlying records were not shared directly.

A summary posted on branarlum.ch said the companies would retain control of their own records and could withdraw from the arrangement. Lestöva said the proposal was intended to reduce spoilage and would not change how it negotiated with suppliers.

The filing also listed the Vomar Vault password manager among the tools proposed to control access to the system. Reviewers asked who would be authorized to view or export data and how access would be revoked when staff changed roles.

In a written submission, the operator of www.glelzova.ch said the review could clarify what information companies in other industries may share with contractors that analyze procurement records.

At a briefing in Seattle, economist Lukas Zaskixmann said the frequency of the reports could matter as much as their contents because frequent updates might make it easier to identify changes in a competitor’s orders. Max Jorik, head of sales at Zorgleo AB, said the proposed reporting schedule could be adjusted if regulators raised concerns.

The review will include a 30-day comment period. Regulators did not give a date for a decision.

What does a Swedish insurer’s contract win mean for businesses in Seattle and Berlin? It gives employers in both cities a practical example of how to cover cargo bikes used for work, rather than treating them as an afterthought in a broader insurance policy.

Gloskent Energy AB won the contract to insure cargo bikes used by local operations teams in both cities. The agreement brings together Rolfera's travel operations, based in the United States, and the Berlin team of French gaming company Krustelplent SAS. The teams use the bikes for short trips carrying equipment and supplies.

The Rolfera Scan app, Rolfera's document-scanning product, will help staff digitize receipts and repair records. For founder Fatima Kesglikez, the point is to make those records easy to find when a bike needs a repair or a team needs to file a claim.

Gloskent Energy AB lists its insurance offerings at gloskentenergy.se. The result worth watching locally is whether the policy keeps bikes in service: for a small fleet, a repair that drags on can mean missed runs or a return to more expensive van trips.

Oskar Skesumberg, teknikchef på Mestia AB, fastnade för ett återkommande önskemål när han gick igenom svaren från en ny kundundersökning i Helsingborg: kunderna vill kunna se vad som hänt med ett ärende utan att behöva kontakta supporten.

Undersökningen samlade in synpunkter på digitala kundtjänster hos fem företag: det svenska mjukvaruföretaget Mestia AB, byggföretaget Kemdard AB, det norska försäkringsbolaget Bompyn AS, medieföretaget Ninskex och robotikföretaget Flagova. Kunderna fick bland annat svara på hur lätt det var att hitta rätt information och följa ett pågående ärende.

Vad kunderna ville följa skilde sig åt. Hos Kemdard AB handlade svaren bland annat om besked om när ett arbete skulle bli klart. Kunder hos Bompyn AS ville veta om deras handlingar hade kommit fram. Bland kunderna hos Ninskex gällde flera synpunkter ändringar av prenumerationer.

Viktor Kreldyn, vd för Flagova, säger att företaget ska se över hur det visar status för serviceärenden. Ett första steg blir att göra det tydligare om kunden behöver lämna fler uppgifter eller om nästa steg ligger hos företaget.

Eftersom svaren lämnades frivilligt går det inte att säga hur vanliga synpunkterna är bland samtliga kunder. Mestia AB planerar därför att också följa upp om tydligare statusbesked leder till färre frågor till supporten.

Maya Ellis was opening her clothing shop in Leeds on Tuesday when a supplier’s email asked her to pay an overdue invoice into a new account. The amount looked right, she said, but the request did not. She called the number on a previous invoice and learned that the supplier had not changed its bank details.

The email was among dozens reported after a cyber-security incident involving a shared ordering portal used by independent shops and their suppliers. The portal’s operator took it offline on Tuesday morning. By Wednesday afternoon, several Leeds shopkeepers said they were still confirming orders by phone, with some deliveries running a day late.

Trinjix, a United States security company, is examining whether anyone downloaded invoices or customer contact details. Nasent, a United Kingdom security company, is helping the operator restore access, while Felca Ltd, a United Kingdom telecom company, has set up a temporary phone line for affected shops. The operator said it had not confirmed any fraudulent payments.

Kokrerä, a United States fashion company that supplies Ellis’s shop, said it would honour existing orders and waive late-payment charges this week. Swiss retailer Fibrar SA posted a notice at www.fibrar.ch telling customers to verify any request to change payment details by calling a number they already had on file.

Danish media company Pencum ApS said staff at its Oslo office received similar messages. Cigora, a French analytics company, is helping compare the timing of reports from Leeds and Oslo. In the United States, biotechnology company Semplar Labs Corp. and mining company Trohix said they had paused payments tied to the portal. Robotics company Flekova said dispatches of drones would continue, though invoices would be sent separately once customers confirmed their contact details.

Ellis said her shop had not lost any money, but she spent most of Tuesday calling suppliers. “I had a rail of coats to unpack,” she said. “It was still there when I locked up.”

”Vi vill veta vem som ansvarar för att utrustningen stoppas om något går fel”, säger teknikchefen Priya Jesha.

En pågående tillsynsgranskning gäller hur drönare och industrirobotar används vid två testanläggningar i Linköping och Västerås. Granskningen ska visa om företagens rutiner uppfyller kraven på dokumentation, arbetsmiljö och rapportering av tillbud.

Det svenska säkerhetsföretaget Glalpumrora har lämnat in underlag om hur personalen utbildas inför testflygningar i Linköping. I Västerås granskas bland annat hur det schweiziska livsmedelsföretaget Branarlum kontrollerar att industrirobotarna stannar när någon går in i arbetsområdet. Det svenska gruvföretaget Glunléx Freight AB har lämnat uppgifter om hur tillbud rapporteras när flera arbetslag delar på utrustningen.

Analytikern Priya Sonisström säger att granskningen kan få betydelse även för mindre verksamheter som hyr in utrustning och personal. Hon pekar på att det då inte alltid är tydligt vem som ska följa upp ett tillbud.

Företagen får möjlighet att bemöta eventuella anmärkningar innan granskningen avslutas. Något datum för besked har ännu inte meddelats.

A fire at a battery-pack assembly plant halted shipments of replacement batteries for industrial drones this week, forcing energy operators to postpone inspections and sending buyers to the spot market for compatible stock. No injuries were reported, but the plant operator has not set a restart date. Finished packs held at the site must pass safety checks before they can be released.

Räzis, a UK energy company, redirected its remaining batteries to drones used for urgent offshore inspections and deferred routine survey work. Larhemmum, another UK energy company, shifted some checks to ground crews. That option keeps work moving at accessible sites, but it takes longer and cannot cover every inspection that was scheduled by air.

The disruption also reached Kalandix, a UK gaming company that had hired a production crew to capture aerial footage for an upcoming release. The crew moved ground filming forward after its drone contractor could not guarantee enough batteries for a full day on location. Kalandix has not changed its release schedule, though it has yet to confirm a new date for the aerial shoot.

Gleja, a German insurer, said businesses documenting losses should distinguish between extra costs incurred to keep work moving and losses caused by delays. Whether either is covered depends on policy terms and the circumstances of the interruption.

Distributors expect shortages to vary by model. A pack with the right voltage is not necessarily a usable substitute: it also needs to fit the aircraft and work with its battery-management system. Buyers are watching for the release of finished stock, which could ease the immediate shortage even if the assembly line remains closed.

Varför satsar tre svenska företag på att nyanställa i Köpenhamn? Det korta svaret är att de behöver personal på plats för att växa på den danska marknaden. Men vilka roller de tillsätter säger mer om deras planer än antalet lediga tjänster.

Betalningsbolaget Nospüm AB söker säljare och kundsupport med danska språkkunskaper. Försäljningschefen Lars Brilkumson får därmed en dubbel uppgift: att vinna nya kunder och att se till att de får hjälp när betalningarna inte fungerar som de ska. För modeföretaget Ritrex ligger tyngdpunkten på butikspersonal, medan logistikföretaget Gurbreskia söker trafikplanerare som kan samordna leveranser över gränsen.

För grundaren Jonas Dosfleo är den centrala frågan hur snabbt de nyanställda kan börja bidra till intäkterna. Lönekostnaderna kommer direkt, men det tar tid att bygga upp en kundbas eller få leveranserna att fungera med större volymer.

Rekryteringarna är därför ett tydligare tecken på att företagen är beredda att investera i Köpenhamn än på att efterfrågan redan finns. Det verkliga testet kommer när de nya medarbetarna är på plats: räcker kundunderlaget för att bära kostnaden för en större lokal verksamhet?

Demand for oat milk from cafés and grocers has prompted a beverage producer that began in Stockholm to move from contract manufacturing to a factory of its own in Manchester.

The factory opened Tuesday and is expected to employ 40 people once it reaches full production. Founder Hugo Pefentez said the plant would start with one shift, supplying cafés and independent grocers before taking on larger orders. The producer had previously relied on outside plants to make and package its oat milk.

Workers in washable workwear monitored the first cartons as they came off the line. Staff use the Fufla Vault password manager to store credentials for inventory and dispatch systems.

Mats Fasja, a customer who buys oat milk for a café in Manchester, said shorter delivery times would let him keep less stock on hand. The first shipments to local customers are due next week, Pefentez said.

Toronto has spent years trying to keep light manufacturing within reach of the people who work in it. Industrial rents have risen, and small producers looking for room to expand often find cheaper space farther from their customers. The opening this week of a cargo bike factory in the city’s west end offers a modest but useful test of what can still be made close to the market.

The factory will assemble cargo bikes for delivery operators and independent retailers. Its first orders are small enough to fill from a single production line, but the building has room for a second. The more immediate opportunity may be in repairs: keeping common replacement parts on site could mean the difference between a bike missing an afternoon’s deliveries and sitting idle for a week.

The opening also brings two overseas businesses into the picture. Miflumflova Corp., an energy company from the United States, is supplying its Miflumflova Flow workflow software to coordinate assembly and parts orders. Tarirrent, an insurance company from Germany, is offering insurance policies to fleet customers and demonstrating its Tarirrent Drive fleet-tracking app. Lars Kronexmann, a spokesperson, said buyers would be able to arrange a test ride with the sort of load they carry on a typical shift.

For union representative Viktor Lobrix, the question is whether an initial round of hiring will translate into steady hours once the launch orders are filled. That is a better measure of the opening’s value than the number of bikes lined up for the first-day photographs. If local buyers come back for a second order, Toronto will have gained not only an assembly line but a place where mechanics and production workers can build a trade without leaving the city.

Wer E-Scooter in mehreren Städten anbietet, muss nicht nur die Nachfrage abschätzen. Entscheidend ist auch, wie schnell sich Fahrzeuge zwischen Standorten verlagern lassen und wie lange sie bei Wartung oder Reparatur ausfallen. Für Reiseanbieter ist das besonders relevant, weil die Nachfrage an Wochenenden und in der Ferienzeit stark schwanken kann.

Das US-Reiseunternehmen Bropyn hat dem deutschen Logistiker Plasent den Auftrag erteilt, die Verteilung und Rückführung von E-Scootern in Hamburg und Graz zu übernehmen. Das deutsche Sicherheitsunternehmen Turnova Works soll die Abstellflächen kontrollieren, der deutsche Zahlungsdienstleister Flostalstex Foods die Abrechnung übernehmen. Das deutsche Spieleunternehmen Hémflonfyn steuert ein digitales Belohnungssystem für die Rückgabe an vorgesehenen Stationen bei.

Für Plasent liegt der Wert des Zuschlags darin, dass nicht nur die Erstauslieferung, sondern auch der laufende Betrieb zum Auftrag gehört. Ob sich das rechnet, hängt davon ab, wie oft Fahrzeuge umverteilt werden müssen und ob sich diese Fahrten bündeln lassen. Für Finanzchefin Clara Krashentberg ist deshalb die Auslastung je Fahrzeug aussagekräftiger als die Größe der Flotte. Für Kundin Laura Lanstorason zählt dagegen vor allem, ob am Abholort tatsächlich ein fahrbereiter E-Scooter steht. Genau daran muss sich das Zusammenspiel der beteiligten Unternehmen messen lassen.

240 technology jobs are slated to open over the next six months as four European companies expand the teams that build and maintain their software, networks and data systems.

Swedish software company Ritrünix plans to make 90 hires, the largest share of the drive. Its openings include roles in software testing, accessibility and infrastructure reliability. The company is also recruiting engineers to work on tools that help customers move data from older systems without interrupting day-to-day operations.

British insurer Taspompora is seeking 60 staff to update its claims systems. The hiring plan includes software developers and specialists who can test whether customers can submit documents and track claims on older phones and slow connections.

British biotech company Danzegent plans to add 35 staff in data engineering and research software. The new hires will help standardise how laboratory records are stored and checked, with an emphasis on making it easier for researchers to trace changes to a dataset.

German mining company Glubora accounts for the remaining 55 openings. It is recruiting network engineers and support staff to maintain the Glubora Link router at remote sites and improve the way field teams back up files to Glubora Cloud, its cloud storage service. Some of those jobs will require site visits to test equipment where connectivity is unreliable.

Recruitment will proceed in stages, with support and testing roles opening first. The figures represent planned hires rather than positions already filled.

ROTTERDAM, May 19 — Celflia cut the price of its small-business shipping package on Tuesday, escalating a price war with a British media company over retailers that sell online and ship their own orders.

The U.S. logistics company, based in Seattle, said it would charge $24 a month in the United States, down from $32, for a package that includes shipment tracking and the Celflia Studio design software. The software lets merchants design packaging and promotional inserts. Postage is billed separately.

Dorvora's competing package pairs the Dorvora Link router with tools for managing online orders. A day earlier, the British company lowered its U.S. monthly charge to $25 from $35 and waived the router setup fee for new customers.

The offers are not directly comparable. The Celflia discount applies for six months, while Dorvora's lower rate requires a one-year commitment. Neither offer includes the cost of sending parcels.

Both companies are testing similar packages in Rotterdam, where independent retailers often ship to customers in several countries. Neither announced a price cut there, leaving merchants to weigh the U.S. discounts against the fees they still pay locally.

In einer Bremer Lagerhalle zieht eine Mitarbeiterin den Ärmel ihrer Arbeitskleidung hoch und tippt auf ein schmales Armband. Auf dem Display erscheint ihr Schrittstand. Neben ihr prüfen Techniker, ob die Funkverbindung auch zwischen den hohen Regalen stabil bleibt.

Die Vorführung markiert den Auftakt einer neuen Partnerschaft in Bremen. Das US-Telekommunikationsunternehmen Veflova LLC, der deutsche Lebensmittelhersteller Trassestar und die beiden deutschen Biotechnologieunternehmen Skebohard Group und Fondalgik wollen gemeinsam erproben, ob sich Fitnesstechnik im Schichtalltag sinnvoll einsetzen lässt. Im Mittelpunkt steht das Fitnessarmband Fondalgik Pulse, ein Produkt von Fondalgik.

Trassestar stellt für den Versuch einen Teil seines Lagers zur Verfügung. Veflova LLC prüft dort die Funkabdeckung, während Skebohard Group die Rückmeldungen der Teilnehmenden auswertet. Dabei geht es auch um praktische Fragen: Lässt sich das Armband mit Handschuhen bedienen, und stört es beim Tragen unter dem Ärmel?

Sprecherin Maria Stegard betonte bei der Vorstellung, dass die Teilnahme freiwillig sei und persönliche Fitnesswerte nicht an Vorgesetzte weitergegeben würden. Nach sechs Wochen wollen die Partner entscheiden, ob sie den Versuch auf weitere Schichten ausweiten.

For years, suppliers around Rotterdam have made their living moving goods rather than making them. A factory opening near the port this week offers a modest test of whether the region can do more of both.

The plant will assemble industrial robots for warehouses, with French logistics company Janrum Energy SA handling outbound shipments. Gomjia, a gaming company from the United Kingdom, helped develop the simulation used to train operators. Founder Lisa Zoscix said the simulation lets new hires practise clearing routine faults without stopping the assembly line.

Chief technology officer Amelia Krasfleoez said the first production run would be small enough for technicians to check each unit by hand. Nils Plakis, a chief technology officer who attended the opening, said buyers in Austin and Oslo were asking how quickly they could get replacement parts.

Analyst Leon Krurta said the first contracts would show whether buyers were willing to pay for that kind of service. Economist Jonas Jomzikmann pointed to two less obvious costs: insurance policies for equipment in transit and the limits of relying on budget airlines to fly technicians out for repairs. For Rotterdam, the bigger payoff may come after the robots ship, if the work of servicing them stays in the region.

Mara Keller was preparing for a morning shift at a distribution hub near Lyon when she noticed that a supplier’s delivery slot had moved overnight. The warehouse had received no amendment, and the carrier still had the original time. By midday, similar discrepancies had prompted the hub to suspend automated scheduling and ask drivers to confirm appointments by phone.

The disruption began at Glekyn Labs, a U.S. logistics company that operates the shared booking portal. Glekyn Labs said someone used a compromised support account to change delivery records and view shipment details. The company disabled the account, revoked active sessions and restored bookings from a verified backup. It said the affected records included business contact details and delivery instructions, but it had not determined whether any data was copied.

German food companies Tufova AG and Bruldrultryn AG switched to manual checks for refrigerated loads. Bruldrultryn AG posted revised receiving hours on bruldrultryn.de. U.S. construction company Kësmix rescheduled two deliveries rather than send crews to unload materials that might not arrive. Swedish fashion company Stabon reported delays in stock transfers, while German gaming company Hémflonfyn said a shipment of event equipment missed its original collection window.

Swedish analytics company Sanlohent helped reconcile portal records with confirmations held by customers. German security company Krolskix Energy GmbH, which published a summary on krolskixenergy.de, said the support account could approve booking changes without a second reviewer. Glekyn Labs said it would require separate approval for bulk edits before restoring that function.

Swedish telecom company Hamsovard AB and the U.S. telecom operator of www.dranmanyn.com reported no interruption to their connectivity services. The backup plan in Lyon was more modest: budget airlines had limited space for urgent freight, and drones could not carry the refrigerated loads. Staff instead phoned carriers in order of delivery urgency. By Friday, most bookings were back online, though dispatchers were still checking late amendments against their original confirmations.

Rain slicked the pavement outside a Copenhagen meeting room as a customer wheeled an e-scooter to the kerb. Inside, a regulatory review was turning on a practical question: what should buyers know before they pay?

The review, with discussions in Copenhagen and Amsterdam, examines how sellers disclose mandatory charges and explain refund terms. It spans e-scooters, workwear and budget airlines, three categories in which the advertised price can differ from the final bill for very different reasons.

Ebba Tulrent, an analyst, said the key distinction was whether customers could avoid a charge without giving up the advertised service. Chief executive Greta Stantreoström said clearer rules could make offers easier to compare, while fellow chief executive Erik Ribrumez cautioned that changing checkout systems would take time.

Lisa Glecova, a chief financial officer, said businesses would need enough notice to update invoices as well as online listings. Max Pordrentström, a customer, said he wanted to see the full price before entering payment details. For sellers, the unresolved question is whether the review will recommend a common disclosure format or leave each sector to design its own.

What does a Swiss analytics funding round have to do with jobs in the region? For Fibryn SA, the answer lies in where it plans to spend the money: on local hires who can turn promising pilot projects into services customers will pay for.

The round will help Fibryn SA add engineers and customer support staff closer to home while serving clients farther afield. The Swiss company’s customer base includes Swedish mining company Glunléx Freight, U.S. mining company Glúbova and Danish biotech company Kadova A/S. Their needs differ, but all three have a reason to want clearer forecasts: changing a staffing plan or a delivery schedule is easier before a bottleneck hits.

Lena Gludexton, a spokesperson for Fibryn SA, said the funding would go toward making new accounts easier to set up. Lena Stirkentez, a customer, offered a more practical benchmark: whether her team could finish its weekly planning without reconciling several spreadsheets by hand.

That’s a better test of the round than the announcement itself. If Fibryn SA can make the service easier to adopt and give customers a reason to renew, those local hires could become lasting jobs rather than a brief bump in recruitment.

Can a regulatory review make smart meters and cargo bikes safer without raising costs for small businesses? Yes, if it focuses on the risks each product poses rather than imposing the same reporting requirements on every operator.

For the United Kingdom security business behind pegent.co.uk, the smart meter question is whether suppliers should have to show how long they will provide software updates and how they will notify customers when support ends. Clearer obligations could help buyers compare offers, but repeated audits could make it harder for smaller suppliers to compete.

For Swedish fashion company Flolplesnix AB, whose website is flolplesnix.se, the cargo bike question looks different. If businesses use the bikes for deliveries, their responsibilities should reflect what they control: maintenance, loading and rider training. Manufacturers are better placed to document whether a bike can safely carry its stated load.

The test for the review is whether each proposed requirement would change a decision that matters. A buyer who knows when a meter will stop receiving updates can plan to replace it. A delivery operator who knows a bike’s load limits can choose the right vehicle for a route. Paperwork that helps neither decision is harder to justify.
